title: Fix automation storage and result review findings
body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Addresses the remaining review findings from #327110. Automation result buttons could interpret user-controlled names as codicons, restored application storage could leave in-memory automation state stale after a successful CAS, and agent-triggered mutations could commit after cancellation or disablement during asynchronous storage work.

- Renders the watch icon independently so automation names remain literal while preserving button accessibility and styling.
- Always adopts the authoritative result of a successful CAS, including after a lower-revision storage restore, while still rejecting stale cross-window notifications.
- Adds an optional pre-CAS mutation guard for agent configure/delete operations and rechecks it before every retry without changing scheduler or runner mutations. Cancellation after atomic CAS begins still reports the committed write as successful.

Tests:
- `npm run typecheck-client`
- Focused chat automation result test
- Full AutomationService and AutomationTools test files (60 tests)
- `npm run valid-layers-check`
- `npm run precommit`

title: Defer the Copilot CLI client restart until every chat is idle
body:
Fixes #327362

## The hang

`CopilotAgent._restartClientIfStartupConfigChanged()` disposed every SDK session and stopped the Copilot CLI client the moment a startup-only config value changed — even with a turn in flight. A session disposed mid-turn stops producing the SDK events that finalize its protocol turn, so the client was left with a turn that never completed, cancelled, or errored: a spinner with no output, no error, and no recovery short of a reload.

From the reported bundle, the session was ~20 minutes into a turn:

```
09:26:44  Tool started: apply_patch          <- model still working
09:27:06  [Copilot] Startup config changed (sessionSync=true), restarting CopilotClient
09:27:07  session.shutdown; CLI subprocess exits
          ...no chat/turnComplete, chat/turnCancelled, or chat/error ever sent
11:36     user exports logs; session still shows as running
```

The agent host itself was healthy — it kept serving a different session for another two hours. Only the session with the in-flight turn was orphaned.

`chat.sessionSync.enabled` is experiment-driven (`experiment: { mode: 'auto' }`) and policy-controlled (`CopilotSessionSync`), so it can flip with **no user action at all**. Here it landed 4s after a managed-settings fetch 404'd and fell back to local-only policy.

The original implementation only restarted when idle (#317390); #319430 removed the `_sessions.size === 0` guard so a toggle would take effect immediately, and later PRs added more triggers (`enterpriseHost`, `copilotSdkLogLevel`, `systemProxy`) to the same unguarded path.

## The fix

**Defer the restart until every chat is idle.** `_requestClientRestart()` runs it immediately when nothing is in flight, and otherwise parks the reason and logs `Deferring CopilotClient restart (…) until N in-flight turn(s) finish`. Parked restarts drain when a chat's turn ends and after `_releaseSessionResources` (a disposed session never reports a turn ending, so disposal drains it too). `_stopClient()` clears them — any stop satisfies a pending restart, since the next `_ensureClient` reads the values fresh. That's also why applying the restart late is always correct.

The CAPI-proxy restart had the identical hazard and now goes through the same path.

**One choke point for "turn ended".** `CopilotAgentSession._clearActiveTurn()` replaces every `_currentTurn = undefined` and notifies the agent through a new `onTurnEnded` option. The agent hops off the current stack with `queueMicrotask` before restarting, since the callback fires from inside the session's own SDK event handling and the restart disposes that session.

**A failed `send()` releases its turn.** Several throw paths left `_currentTurn` set forever; the host finalizes the protocol turn with a `ChatError`, but the session still looked busy. Pre-existing (it already blocked idle eviction), but this change would have escalated it to permanently parking every later restart, so `send()` is now a thin guard around `_send()` that clears the turn on rejection.

## Interaction with #327408

That PR landed on this same code while this was in review, and the merge is included here:

- It re-enumerated models right after the restart. Since the restart now happens later, that moved into `_applyPendingClientRestart` so it still runs whenever the restart actually fires — its `re-enumerates models after a startup-config restart` test passes against the relocated code.
- It also reworked `_stopClient` to dedupe concurrent stops. That version is kept, with `_pendingClientRestartReasons.clear()` at the top — synchronously, before the dedup check — so a concurrent apply bails instead of stopping a client already being torn down.

## Tradeoffs

- While a restart is parked, the client keeps running with stale config until the next quiet point.
- If a turn never ends, the restart never applies — the setting simply doesn't take effect, which is strictly better than killing live work.
- #327362 also suggests finalizing the turn on session disposal as defense-in-depth. Not included here; this PR removes the path that reaches it.

## Validation

- `typecheck-client`, `valid-layers-check`, eslint, and the hygiene hook are clean.
- 3452 agent-host tests pass.
- 6 new tests: deferral while busy, multi-chat deferral, drain on disposal, no double-stop, the turn-ended hook firing on both normal completion and abort, and the failed-send release. Each was verified to **fail** against the old behavior rather than assumed to be meaningful.

(Written by Copilot)

commit_messages:
['Defer the Copilot CLI client restart until every chat is idle

A startup-only config change (session sync, SDK log level, enterprise
host, system proxy) tore down every SDK session and stopped the client
immediately. A session disposed mid-turn stops producing the events that
finalize its protocol turn, so the client was left with a turn that never
completed, cancelled, or errored - the session spun forever with no error
and no way to recover but a reload. `chat.sessionSync.enabled` is
experiment- and policy-driven, so this could kill a running turn with no
user action at all; that is what a reported ~2h hang turned out to be.

Park the restart instead and apply it once no chat has an in-flight turn.
The values are read fresh on the next client start, so applying the
restart late is always correct. The CAPI proxy restart goes through the
same path since it had the identical hazard.

Also release the turn when `send()` rejects: nothing else closes a turn
whose send never reached the SDK loop, and such a chat would look busy
forever - blocking idle eviction before this change, and parking every
later restart after it.

Fixes #327362

(Written by Copilot)

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>', "Merge remote-tracking branch 'origin/main' into roblou/agents/investigate-session-hanging-issue

# Conflicts:
#	src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotAgent.ts", 'Contain a failing onTurnEnded callback

The callback runs from SDK event handling and from the `send()` failure
path, where an escaping error would replace the send error we are
propagating. The turn is already cleared before it runs, so log and
continue rather than unwinding through the caller.

(Written by Copilot)

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>']

title: Fix plan-review leak on abort in Copilot Agent Session
body:
This pull request addresses a confirmed defect in the Copilot Agent Session where pending plan reviews were not being cleared upon aborting a turn. The changes made include:

- Updated the `abort()` method to resolve and remove pending plan reviews, preventing orphaned callbacks from accumulating across subsequent prompts.
- Added a regression test to ensure that aborting a pending plan review correctly resolves its callback and that late UI responses are ignored.

Validation steps included running type-checks, all Copilot Agent Session tests, hygiene checks, and layer checks.

Related to #326653. A self-hosted reproduction confirmed that repeatedly sending a new prompt during plan review accumulated unresolved plan-review callbacks and redisplayed the existing plan. The permanent unresponsive state was not reproduced, so this PR intentionally does not claim to fully close the issue.

(Written by Copilot)
author: roblourens
review_comments: [{'user': 'Copilot', 'body': 'This test currently awaits `responsePromise` before calling `respondToUserInputRequest(...)` due to object-literal evaluation order. That means it does not actually validate that a *late* response cannot affect the still-pending plan-review promise; it only validates that responding after completion returns `false`. To cover the intended regression, compute `lateResponseHandled` before awaiting `responsePromise` (or run them in parallel with `Promise.all`) so the late response attempt happens while the plan-review resolution is being observed.', 'created_at': '2026-07-25T19:21:26+00:00', 'path': 'src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotAgentSession.test.ts', 'position': 22}, {'user': 'Copilot', 'body': 'The test name says \\"rejects\\" but the assertion expects the plan review to resolve with `{ approved: false }`. Consider renaming to match the observed behavior (e.g., \\"abort resolves and clears a pending plan review\\"), or adjust the expectation to assert an actual promise rejection if rejection is the intended contract.', 'created_at': '2026-07-25T19:21:26+00:00', 'path': 'src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotAgentSession.test.ts', 'position': 1}]

title: Fix flaky skill watch test: add non-recursive watchers on skill subdirectories
body:
In `scan` mode, the `watch skill file changes` integration test flakily times out because content-only modifications to `SKILL.md` (two levels deep: `skillsDir/skill-name/SKILL.md`) are sometimes not detected on macOS CI VMs.

## Root cause

Skills were watched exclusively via a recursive `@parcel/watcher` on `skillsDir`. On macOS VMs, this recursive watcher can fail to fire for content-only changes deep in the tree. Agents don't have this problem because they use a non-recursive `fs.watch`/kqueue watcher on a directory whose direct children are the watched files.

## Fix

In `_scanRoot` for `DiscoveredType.Skill`, add an explicit **non-recursive** watcher on each discovered skill subdirectory (trigger = the `SKILL.md` file URI):

```typescript
// before: only recursive watcher on skillsDir
addWatch(watchRootUris, rootUri, root.recursive ?? false, rootUri);

// after: also add non-recursive watcher on each skill's subdirectory
addWatch(watchRootUris, child.resource, false, skillFile);
```

When `SKILL.md` is modified, `e.affects(skillFile)` returns `true` immediately — a more specific, reliable trigger that doesn't depend on `@parcel/watcher`'s recursive event delivery. This mirrors how `discover` mode watches individual skill file paths.

## Tests

- Updated `installs watchers for roots that contain discovered customizations` to assert skill subdirectories (e.g. `.github/skills/bar`) are now watched non-recursively in addition to the recursive `skillsDir` watcher.
- Added `fires onDidChange when an existing SKILL.md file is modified` to directly validate content-change detection via the new non-recursive watcher.

<!-- START COPILOT CODING AGENT SUFFIX -->

- Fixes #327447

title: Set AI_AGENT for all agent sessions, not just runInTerminal
body:
Fixes #326069

## What

`AI_AGENT` is a cross-vendor environment-variable convention that `git` and `gh` inherit, and which GitHub's data team uses to attribute downstream activity (commits, PRs) back to the AI surface that originated it. jolitz asked that every GitHub Copilot surface set a distinct value of the form `github_copilot_[SURFACE]`, and cwebster-99 clarified that the intent is to track **all** agent usage in VS Code, not just the CLI.

Before this change VS Code set `AI_AGENT` in exactly one place — the Local harness's `runInTerminal` tool — so every agent-host session was invisible to the metric.

This adds a single shared constant and sets the marker at every layer of the spawn chain, so the guarantee doesn't depend on one inheritance path staying intact.

New module `src/vs/platform/chat/common/aiAgentEnv.ts` exports `AiAgentEnvVar` / `AiAgentEnvValue` (`github_copilot_vscode_agent`), consumed by:

| File | Why it's needed here |
|---|---|
| `electronAgentHostStarter.ts` | root of the desktop agent-host spawn chain |
| `nodeAgentHostStarter.ts` | root of the server/remote chain |
| `copilotAgent.ts` | the CLI env is rebuilt from scratch and a strip loop deletes all `VSCODE_*`/`ELECTRON_*` keys, so it must be re-set afterwards |
| `claudeSdkOptions.ts` | the Claude SDK **replaces** the subprocess env rather than merging, and proxied (Copilot-routed) mode deliberately builds a sparse env — inheritance alone would drop it. Also set in `settings.env`, which the CLI layers onto Bash-tool commands |
| `codexLaunchConfig.ts` | Codex filters its shell tool's env through `shell_environment_policy`, so it also needs `-c shell_environment_policy.set.AI_AGENT=...` |
| `agentHostTerminalManager.ts` | AHP terminal pty env |
| `toolTerminalCreator.ts` | pre-existing Local-harness implementation, switched from a string literal to the shared constant (no behavior change) |

Single value for all harnesses (P1). Per-harness granularity (`github_copilot_vscode_agent_claude`, …) is deliberately deferred.

## Scenarios covered

- Agent host process itself (desktop + server/remote)
- Agent-host **Copilot CLI** sessions
- Agent-host **Codex** sessions
- Agent-host **Claude** sessions (partially — see caveat)
- Agent-host terminals (`chat.agentHost.customTerminalTool.enabled`)
- Local harness `runInTerminal` (unchanged behavior, now sharing the constant)

## Validation

Static: `typecheck-client`, `valid-layers-check`, `eslint` and `compile` are clean; 65 targeted unit tests pass.

Runtime, against a Code OSS build from these sources (Agents window). The probe has the agent run a script that writes the marker vars to a file, which is then read directly from disk rather than parsed out of the chat response:

| Surface | `AI_AGENT` observed by the agent's shell tool |
|---|---|
| Agent host utility process (`ps eww`) | `github_copilot_vscode_agent` |
| Copilot CLI subprocess (`ps eww`) | `github_copilot_vscode_agent` |
| **AH Copilot CLI** shell tool | `github_copilot_vscode_agent` |
| **AH Codex** shell tool | `github_copilot_vscode_agent` |
| **AH Claude** bash tool | `claude-code_<version>_agent` (see caveat) |

Additionally:

- Reproduced the full Copilot stdio path standalone (`CopilotClient` + `RuntimeConnection.forStdio`) and confirmed the marker survives **with** MXC sandbox auto-detection (`MXC_BIN_DIR`) and **with** a `sandboxConfig` pushed via `session.rpc.options.update`.
- Verified the new Codex `-c` argument against the real `codex` binary (`codex-cli 0.142.0`) via `codex sandbox`: the key is accepted, is genuinely necessary (an `inherit = "core"` policy strips an inherited `AI_AGENT`), and it **merges into** rather than clobbers a user's existing `shell_environment_policy.set` table.

## Caveats

1. **Claude re-stamps the variable for its own bash tool.** The bundled `claude` binary overwrites `AI_AGENT` with `claude-code_<version>_agent` when it invokes its agent bash tool. Our value is present in the Claude process and in everything else it spawns, but Claude's bash tool asserts its own vendor marker. This is not overridable from VS Code by setting env alone and would need an upstream change.
2. **The extension-host Copilot CLI harness is not covered.** That harness is being deprecated in favor of the agent-host one, so no change was made there.
3. **The metric counts users who make a `git`/`gh` commit.** A session that only edits files still won't register — that's inherent to how the signal is collected, not something this PR changes.

## How to validate manually

1. Enable the agent-host harnesses in Settings:
   ```jsonc
   "chat.agentHost.enabled": true,
   // makes the *agent-host* Copilot session type the one that surfaces,
   // instead of the extension-host one
   "chat.agents.copilotCli.hideExtensionHost": true,
   // only if you also want to check Codex
   "chat.agentHost.codexAgent.enabled": true
   ```
   Restart VS Code (the agent host process must be restarted to pick these up).

2. Create a scratch folder with this script in it:
   ```sh
   # probe.sh
   #!/bin/sh
   echo "AI_AGENT=$AI_AGENT"
   ```

3. Open the Agents window, start a **new** session in that folder, and pick the session type from the `with …` picker (**Copilot**, **Codex**, or **Claude**).

4. Send: `Run this shell command: sh ./probe.sh` and approve the confirmation.

5. Expected output: `AI_AGENT=github_copilot_vscode_agent` for Copilot and Codex. For Claude, expect `claude-code_<version>_agent` (see caveat 1).

Notes for verification:
- Be sure to use a **new** session created after the restart — a resumed session may be served by the older harness.
- If the composer placeholder still says "Run tasks in the background with the Copilot CLI", you're on the extension-host harness; double-check `chat.agents.copilotCli.hideExtensionHost` and restart.
- Cross-check without a chat at all: find the agent host process and its CLI child and dump their environments, e.g. on macOS/Linux `ps eww -p <pid> | tr ' ' '\n' | grep AI_AGENT`.

title: sessions: support mouse back/forward buttons in the Agents window
body:
Fixes #327434

## Problem

The mouse back/forward buttons navigate editor history in the main VS Code window, but did nothing in the Agents window — even though the `Alt+Left` / `Alt+Right` keybindings already navigated between sessions there.

## Root cause

The shared mouse handler in `HistoryService.onMouseDownOrUp` calls `goBack()` / `goForward()` on the **editor** history service directly:

```ts
case 3:
    EventHelper.stop(event);
    if (isMouseDown) { this.goBack(); }   // service call, not a command dispatch
```

Because it bypasses command/keybinding resolution entirely, no `when`-clause routing applies. That is exactly why the keyboard path worked while the mouse path did not: the Agents window has its own session history (`SessionsNavigation`, exposed via `ISessionsService.openPreviousSession()` / `openNextSession()`), and the editor history the mouse fell through to is usually empty there.

Note this is not a case of "the Agents window forgot to reuse the editor commands". Both histories are deliberately live in that window — editor history still matters for the docked side pane (Changes multi-diff, Files, file diffs) — and the two are disambiguated by focus via `EditorAreaFocusContext`. The gap is only that mouse buttons don't go through the same dispatch as their keybindings.

## Changes

- **New `SessionsMouseNavigationContribution`** (`src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/browser/sessionsMouseNavigation.ts`): a capture-phase `mousedown` / `mouseup` listener on each workbench container that routes buttons 4/5 to session history when focus is **outside** the editor area. It stops propagation so the shared bubble listener does not also navigate editor history, and suppresses `mouseup` so the browser's own back/forward does not fire.
- **Editor focus is left untouched.** With the editor area focused the events pass through unchanged, so the docked side pane keeps its normal editor-history behavior.
- **Setting is honored.** `workbench.editor.mouseBackForwardToNavigate` still gates the behavior. Its key is now an exported `MOUSE_BACK_FORWARD_NAVIGATION_SETTING` constant in `services/history/common/history.ts`, shared by `HistoryService`, the configuration registration, and the new contribution instead of being duplicated as a string literal.
- **Keybindings:** added `BrowserBack` / `BrowserForward` as secondary bindings for `sessions.goBack` / `sessions.goForward`, matching `NavigateBackwardsAction` / `NavigateForwardAction`.
- **Accessibility:** documented Go Back / Go Forward in the Agents window accessibility help dialog (per the `accessibility` skill's rule that new commands must be discoverable there).
- **Docs:** noted the routing rule in `src/vs/sessions/SESSIONS.md`.

## Tests

New `sessionsMouseNavigation.test.ts` covers the three behaviors that matter:

1. Buttons 4/5 navigate session history once per press, and the event neither bubbles to the shared listener nor reaches browser history.
2. With the editor area focused, events pass through untouched and no session navigation occurs.
3. Toggling `workbench.editor.mouseBackForwardToNavigate` disables/enables handling.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client` — pass
- `npm run valid-layers-check` — pass
- hygiene on all changed files — pass
- `sessionsMouseNavigation.test.ts` — 4 passing
- `sessionNavigation.test.ts` — 18 passing (no regression)
- `historyService.test.ts` — 23 passing (no regression)

## Note for reviewers

A cleaner long-term fix would be to have the `HistoryService` mouse handler dispatch `workbench.action.navigateBack` / `navigateForward` through `ICommandService` so `when` clauses decide the target. Any window contributing higher-weight bindings for those chords would then get mouse support for free, and this sessions-specific listener could be deleted. That touches shared workbench behavior, so I kept this fix scoped — happy to switch approaches if preferred.

(Written by Copilot)

commit_messages:
['Support mouse back/forward buttons in the Agents window

The mouse back/forward buttons navigated editor history but did nothing
in the Agents window, even though the Alt+Left / Alt+Right keybindings
already navigated between sessions there.

The shared `HistoryService` mouse listener calls `goBack()`/`goForward()`
on the editor history service directly, bypassing command and keybinding
resolution. That is why the keyboard path (which is routed by `when`
clauses) worked while the mouse path did not: the Agents window has its
own session history (`SessionsNavigation`), and the editor history it
fell through to is usually empty there.

Add a sessions-owned capture-phase listener that routes buttons 4/5 to
`ISessionsService.openPreviousSession()`/`openNextSession()` while focus
is outside the editor area, stopping propagation so the shared bubble
listener does not also navigate editor history. With the editor area
focused the events pass through unchanged, so the docked side pane
(Changes, Files, diffs) keeps its normal editor-history behavior. The
existing `workbench.editor.mouseBackForwardToNavigate` setting is
honored, and its key is now an exported constant shared by both paths.

Also add `BrowserBack`/`BrowserForward` as secondary keybindings for the
session Go Back/Go Forward actions, matching the editor actions, and
document both in the Agents window accessibility help dialog.

(Written by Copilot)

title: sessions: never select a harness the picker doesn't offer
body:
## Problem

While running the experiment that replaces the extension-host Copilot CLI with the Agent Host one:

```jsonc
"chat.agents.copilotCli.hideExtensionHost": true,
"chat.agentHost.enabled": true,
"chat.agentHost.defaultSessionsProvider": true,
```

switching to an extension-host session in the Agents window and then going back to the new chat page left the **extension-host agent selected**, even though it is hidden from the harness picker. You should never be able to have an agent selected that isn't actually offered in the picker.

## Root cause

Two "remember the previous agent" mechanisms compounded.

**1. The New Session gestures inherit the previous session's harness unconditionally.**

`NewChatInSessionsWindowAction` (the New button and <kbd>Cmd+N</kbd>) passed the active session's `providerId` + `sessionType` straight to `openNewSession`. With the setting on, `CopilotChatSessionsProvider.getSessionTypes()` returns `[]`, so `_resolveProviderForNewSession` throws `does not advertise session type 'copilotcli'` — and `openNewSession` swallows it with only a trace log.

A throwaway unit test against the real `SessionsManagementService` / `SessionsService` confirmed the outcome — nothing is created on *either* provider, the folder is dropped, and the composer lands session-less:

```
activeProviderBefore: 'copilot',  createdOnCopilot: [],  createdOnAgentHost: [],
draftProviderId: undefined,       activeAfter: undefined,
folderTypes: ['local-agent-host/copilotcli']
```

**2. With no session, the picker falls back to the stored pick without validating it.**

`SessionTypePicker._computeCurrentPick()` returned either the session's `{providerId, sessionTypeId}` verbatim or `_readStoredPick()` (`sessions.userSelectedSessionType`) — never checking either against `_folderSessionTypes`, the list the dropdown actually renders. So the remembered `{providerId: 'copilot', sessionTypeId: 'copilotcli'}` shows as selected while being absent from the picker.

## Changes

- **`sessionsManagement.ts`** — new shared `inheritableSessionTarget()` helper: carry the harness over only while `isNewSessionTargetAvailable()` says the folder still offers it, otherwise fall back to the folder's preferred harness.
- **`chat.contribution.ts` / `sessionsService.ts`** — both "carry the harness over" sites (New Session, and the archived-session fallback) now route through that helper. New Session keeps the folder and lets the Agent Host's Copilot serve it.
- **`sessionTypePicker.ts`** — new `_offeredPick()` constrains the displayed pick to the offered types. Applied to the stored pick and to *uncommitted drafts*.
- **`newChatWidget.ts`** — `_replaceDraftOnUnservableHarness()` recreates a restored draft whose harness the folder can no longer serve, so the composer can't show one agent while sending to another.

## Notes for reviewers

Two deliberate carve-outs, both covered by tests:

- A **committed** session keeps displaying the harness it genuinely runs on, even if that harness is no longer offered for *new* sessions — the picker should tell the truth about an existing session.
- An **empty** type list means the folder's providers haven't reported yet (a late-connecting agent host), so the pick/draft is left alone. This preserves the existing late-discovery behaviour that `_scheduleRecreateOnProviderChange` and the "preserves an unavailable initial pick until its provider appears" tests rely on.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client`, hygiene, and `npm run valid-layers-check` are clean.
- All **1659** `src/vs/sessions` unit tests pass, including 4 new regression tests:
  - `a draft never displays a harness the picker no longer offers`
  - `a committed session keeps displaying the harness it runs on`
  - `a stored pick for a hidden harness does not survive into an offering picker`
  - `inheritableSessionTarget drops a harness the folder no longer offers`

Not verified by running the app: `npm install` fails on `extensions/copilot`'s private registry here (`npm error code E401`), so the extension-host Copilot CLI side isn't buildable in this environment. Everything above is verified at the unit level against the real services. Worth a manual pass with the experiment settings before this leaves draft.

(Written by Copilot)

Fixes #327429

title: Harden Agent Host E2E and protocol integration tests
body:
Hardens the Agent Host E2E and protocol integration tests following the failures reported in [this PR comment](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/327213#issuecomment-5064384775).

## Changes

- use platform-aware protocol operation timeouts with extra Windows and coverage headroom
- register pending JSON-RPC calls before sending to avoid fast-response races
- centralize bounded graceful server shutdown with forced termination fallback
- await server shutdown across protocol suites to avoid process overlap
- track and clean up secondary WebSocket clients on failure paths
- replace wall-clock sleeps with protocol barriers and turn-specific notification matching
- add retry-backed temporary resource cleanup for Windows

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client`
- `npm run precommit`
- Agent Host protocol integration tests: 115 passing, 1 pending
- reported terminal E2E cases for Claude: 2 passing
- reported terminal E2E cases for Copilot: 2 passing
- final code review: no findings

(Written by Copilot)
author: roblourens

body:
- Queued and steering messages were only published from the local chat model, so other connected editors and agent windows could not display server-side changes.
- Attaching an empty local model could incorrectly remove messages already queued by another client. Reconciliation now treats protocol state as authoritative while remaining atomic and idempotent.
- Preserving protocol ids, attachments, deferred cleanup, and yield state keeps queue behavior consistent across clients without re-entrancy guards.
- Adds coverage for cross-client additions, initial hydration, atomic updates, and no-op synchronization.

title: agentHost: Attribute telemetry to initiating window
body:
## Summary

- identify editor and Agents window AHP clients through `initialize.clientInfo`
- decorate existing Agent Host and Copilot CTS telemetry with `initiatorClientType`
- preserve the initiating client for queued turns
- retain attribution across reconnects, falling back to a fresh initialize when the host no longer remembers the client

## Why

An Agent Host process and session can be shared by multiple VS Code windows. Session identity and process-wide common properties therefore cannot reliably identify which window initiated a turn. This adds per-interaction attribution without introducing a new telemetry event.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client`
- `npm run valid-layers-check`
- hygiene checks
- 712 targeted Agent Host tests, plus focused reconnect/service tests

## Review notes

Please pay particular attention to the existing CTS event property name, SDK telemetry callback routing, queued-message attribution lifetime, and reconnect fallback behavior.

(Written by Copilot)

title: Add Claude Opus 5 system prompt
body:
Adds a minimal system prompt for Claude Opus 5, gated behind `github.copilot.chat.claudeOpus5Prompt.enabled` (experiment-based, off by default). When off, Opus 5 falls back to the existing Claude 4.6 Opus prompt.

### The new prompt

Built following Anthropic's guidance for the Claude 5 generation — describe the environment as facts rather than as a list of rules, and put the behavioral weight into scope and correction guidance instead of prohibitions. It keeps six sections: `instructions`, `harness`, `deliveringWork`, `operationalSafety`, `communication`, and `outputFormatting`, plus the MCP, notebook, linkification, and translation pieces the UI depends on.

What's deliberately **not** in it: separate verification passes, over-engineering and comment policies, task-tracking rules, and worked examples. Anthropic's guidance is that this generation handles those with its own judgement, and that verification instructions in particular cause *over*-verification. Context compaction is assumed off for this model, so there's no `contextManagement` section.

### Also in this change

- **Removed the Opus 4.8 and Sonnet 5 prompts** and their settings (`claude48OpusPrompt.enabled`, `claudeSonnet5Prompt.enabled`). Both models now use the Claude 4.6 prompts.
- **Comment-etiquette guidance** added to `AnthropicReminderInstructionsOptimized` rather than to a single prompt, so it reaches every Claude 4.6+ family. This is what moves the 22 snapshots — the added line is the only delta in each.
- **Tool search enabled for `claude-opus-5`.**

following Anthropic's guidance for the Claude 5 generation: describe the

  reaches every Claude 4.6+ family rather than a single prompt.

drafting. Rewrites every affected passage in original wording, keeping
the guidance intact. Verified no shared word sequence of five or more
remains between the branch's added lines and that reference."]

title: agentHost: refresh model catalogs periodically
body:
## Summary

- refresh Agent Host provider model catalogs every 10 minutes from a single host-owned scheduler
- coalesce periodic refreshes while preserving forced refreshes for token, transport, usage-source, and client-generation changes
- refresh Copilot models after CLI restart and prevent stale same-token responses from the previous client generation from publishing
- preserve last-known-good Claude, Codex, and Copilot catalogs after transient refresh failures

Fixes [#327413](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/327413).

## Validation

- TypeScript typecheck
- `npm run valid-layers-check`
- staged-file precommit hygiene
- full Agent Host unit suite: 3427 passing, 0 failing

(Written by Copilot)

title: sessions: Refine the prompt sticky header (styling, navigation, roll)
body:
Polishes the Agents-window prompt timeline **sticky header** (introduced in #326861). All changes are scoped to `src/vs/sessions/contrib/promptTimeline/` (plus a one-line accessibility-help update and a spec note).

### What changed

**Styling — align with the VS Code standard and the session header**
- Replace the hover **underline** on the sticky title with the standard **hover background**, using the chat request-bubble tokens (`--vscode-chat-requestBubbleHoverBackground`), with padding + a control-tier radius for breathing room.
- Give the band the chat request-bubble **background** (composited over the opaque panel base so it stays opaque over scrolling rows).
- Mirror the **session header's box model** so the band lines up with the header's bottom-border line above it: a centered 950 host with the header bar's 10px side padding (`.session-view-centered-content` + `.chat-composite-bar.session-header-bar`), and an inner band that carries the background/border/shadow (like `.chat-composite-bar-header`). A left inset of `codicon size + 6px gap` reproduces the header's status-icon column so the prompt text stays aligned with the title and the prompts below. This also removed a ~1px right-edge "bump" where the previous full-width band overhung the scrollbar gutter.
- Round the band's **bottom corners** (control tier) and add **left + right borders** with an open top, so it reads as anchored to the top of the transcript and closing off at the bottom.

**Navigation — make it consistent**
- Previous/Next now reveal the prompt **row itself** (aligned to the top), exactly like clicking the sticky title and like the dock rail — previously they aligned the following response and pinned the header, which showed only a sliver of the target prompt.
- Removed the navigation-pin machinery; the header now consistently follows scroll tracking and hides after a jump.

**Transition — a lightweight "roll"**
- When the pinned prompt changes while the header is visible, the label text rolls (slide + fade of the outgoing/incoming line) via the Web Animations API, inside a clip viewport. The opaque band stays fixed (a full Explorer-style push-off would overflow above the transcript and clip the band's shadow). Snaps on first appearance/jumps and honors `prefers-reduced-motion`.

### Notes for reviewers
- **Performance:** profiled a scroll-heavy DevTools trace — the roll and reveal animations are 100% GPU-composited (0 composite failures) and the sticky header contributes ~0 to style-recalc/layout (`prompt-timeline` appears in 0 of the 888 `UpdateLayoutTree` events). Total main-thread cost attributable to the band across ~7.3s is ~3ms of paint.
- **Accessibility:** the accessibility-help entry for the prompt timeline was updated to mention activating the pinned title / Previous & Next buttons. The band's `<button>` + toolbar actions keep their labels/roles; transient roll lines are governed by the button's `aria-label`.
- No new tests: this is UI polish on an existing feature. Manual verification suggested on a wide and a narrow window, with reduced motion on/off, and scrolling fast across many prompts.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit_messages:
['sessions: Refine prompt sticky header styling and navigation

- Replace the sticky title hover underline with the chat request bubble
  background and hover color, matching the VS Code standard treatment.
- Give the hover background breathing room (padding + control-tier radius)
  while keeping the label aligned with the prompts underneath.
- Let the header span the full transcript width so the prompt label uses the
  available room before it has to ellipsize.
- Reveal the prompt row itself on Previous/Next (like the dock rail and the
  title), and drop the navigation pin so the header consistently hides after a
  jump instead of covering the top-aligned prompt.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>', 'sessions: Roll the sticky prompt header label on prompt change

When the pinned prompt changes while the sticky header is visible, the
outgoing prompt name slides and fades out while the incoming name slides in
from the scroll direction, using the Web Animations API. The opaque band
stays fixed (translating it would overflow above the transcript and clip its
shadow); only the label text rolls inside a clip viewport. Snaps on first
appearance and jumps, and honors prefers-reduced-motion.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>', "sessions: Constrain the sticky prompt band to the message column

Move the band's background, border, and shadow from the full-width outer
element onto the centered content element (max-width 950, margin auto) so it
matches the transcript's title and prompt column instead of bleeding to the
window edges. This also removes the ~1px bump where the full-width band
overhung the vertical scrollbar gutter on the right.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>", "sessions: Align the sticky prompt band with the session header

Mirror the session header's box model so the band's background lines up with
the header's bottom-border line above it: a centered 950 host with the header
bar's 10px side padding, and an inner band that carries the background,
border, and shadow (like .chat-composite-bar-header). A 22px left inset
reproduces the header's status-icon column so the prompt text stays aligned
with the title and the prompts below.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>", "sessions: Round the sticky prompt band's bottom corners

Add a 4px (control-tier) radius to the bottom corners of the sticky prompt
band so it reads as a rounded control resting on the transcript.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>", 'sessions: Add side borders to the sticky prompt band

Give the band left and right borders (in addition to the bottom) with the
top left open, so the rounded bottom corners read as intentional: the band is
anchored to the top of the transcript and closes off at the bottom. Switch the
border to the stroke-thickness token.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>', "sessions: Address PR review feedback on the sticky prompt header

- Composite the label hover token over the opaque panel base so it matches the
  standard chat bubble hover instead of stacking over the band's own tint.
- Reuse --session-view-centered-content-max-width (with a 950px fallback)

- Keep the SKILL note aligned with the request-bubble hover treatment.
- Shorten two-line method-body comments to one line.

title: agentHost: route steering messages to the chat they were sent in
body:
- Copilot's `setPendingMessages` resolved its target via `_findAnySession`, which always returns the session's default chat. A steering message submitted in a forked (peer) chat was therefore injected into the primary chat's SDK session, steering the wrong conversation and never reaching the intended one.
- Makes the chat URI the single, required addressing argument on `IAgent.setPendingMessages`. Previously the session URI was the primary argument with an optional `chat` override, which left an ambiguous session-addressed form that could silently land in an arbitrary chat. There is no case where pending messages should be set without naming a concrete chat channel.
- Claude and Codex are updated to the new signature so all harnesses share one addressing convention, and `AgentSideEffects` now forwards the chat channel it already has instead of downgrading the default chat to the session URI.

Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/326244

commit_messages:
["agentHost: route steering messages to the chat they were sent in

- Copilot's `setPendingMessages` resolved its target via `_findAnySession`,
  which always returns the session's default chat. A steering message
  submitted in a forked (peer) chat was therefore injected into the primary
  chat's SDK session, steering the wrong conversation and never reaching the
  intended one.
- Makes the chat URI the single, required addressing argument on
  `IAgent.setPendingMessages`. Previously the session URI was the primary
  argument with an optional `chat` override, which left an ambiguous
  session-addressed form that could silently land in an arbitrary chat.
  There is no case where pending messages should be set without naming a
  concrete chat channel.
- Claude and Codex are updated to the new signature so all harnesses share
  one addressing convention, and `AgentSideEffects` now forwards the chat
  channel it already has instead of downgrading the default chat to the
  session URI.

Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/326244

(Commit message generated by Copilot)

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>"]

title: preferences: call Delayer.isTriggered() so Down focuses settings results
body:
## Summary
- Fixes #327360: Down Arrow (and Enter) from Settings search never moved focus into results because `Delayer.isTriggered` was used without calling it. The method reference is always truthy, so `isSearchUpToDate()` always returned false and focus stayed in the search box.
- Call `isTriggered()` in both `isSearchUpToDate` and `focusSearch`, and extract `isSettingsSearchUpToDate(...)` with a `boolean` parameter so omitting `()` is a TypeScript error.
- Bug is cross-platform (reported on macOS). Related one-liner also appears in the larger #326375 F7 navigation PR; this is a minimal dedicated fix.

## Test plan

- [ ] Manual: Open Settings UI, focus search, press **Down** → focus moves into settings tree
- [ ] Manual: Same with **Enter**
- [ ] Manual: Type a query, press Down before debounce settles → focus stays in search; after results update, Down moves focus
- [ ] Manual: Focus search via command / click so `inSettingsSearch` context is set

title: Fix cancelling speech-to-text model preparation
body:
Fixes #327292

When dictation is toggled while the speech-to-text model is still downloading or loading, cancel the active dictation instead of attempting to stop and transcribe. This makes the preparing affordance reversible while preserving the existing stop behavior once recording is ready.

Also updates the Agents window accessibility label/help content and adds regression coverage for the dictation toggle state transitions.

Validation:
- Pre-commit hygiene hook passed
- `git diff --check` passed

The potentially hundreds-of-MB download therefore continues after the user activates Cancel. title: Avoid false positives in dictation cleanup validation
body:
Regression from #327224.

The dictation cleanup faithfulness guard split text only on whitespace and then removed punctuation within each token. Legitimate cleanup such as open source becoming open-source, em-dash formatting, apostrophes, or Unicode accent normalization could therefore look like a wording change and incorrectly fall back to the raw transcript.

This tokenizes Unicode word runs after normalizing accents and apostrophes. It continues to require cleaned words to appear in order and retain at least 60% of the transcript, preserving protection against generated HTML, generated prose, reordered text, and heavy truncation.

Adds focused regression coverage for accepted formatting and rejected generated or meaning-changing output.

title: Fix hydrated image attachment previews
body:
Fixes #327299

## Summary

- reject URI-backed image attachments when coercing serialized inline bytes
- let the image carousel load hydrated attachments from their persisted file resource
- preserve support for contiguous numeric byte maps restored from older serialized sessions

## Why this is correct

Before send, pasted images carry inline `Uint8Array` data. Agent Host intentionally snapshots that data to disk, and history hydration restores the attachment as an image entry whose `value` is a `URI` and whose `references` point to the persisted file.

`coerceImageBuffer` is only responsible for recognizing inline bytes. Its previous object fallback accepted every object, so the seven enumerable fields of a `URI` became seven zero bytes. Because that result was truthy, Images Preview preferred the corrupt inline data and skipped its valid file-resource fallback.

The new validation accepts only the exact legacy serialized-`Uint8Array` shape: contiguous numeric keys starting at `0`, each containing an integer byte from `0` through `255`. Existing `Uint8Array` and `ArrayBuffer` paths are unchanged. URI and other structured objects now return `undefined`, which deliberately lets the existing resource path read the persisted image.

The regression test uses the hydrated shape (`value: URI` plus its resource reference), while the existing numeric-map tests ensure backward compatibility, including reordered numeric keys.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client`
- `npm run valid-layers-check`
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/common/chatImageExtraction.test.ts`
- focused hygiene checks
- reopened a hydrated Agent Host session and confirmed the sent image renders in Images Preview

title: agentHost: support OpenAI subscriptions in Codex
body:
## Summary

- Allow the Agent Host Codex harness to use either the default GitHub Copilot subscription or an existing OpenAI/ChatGPT Codex login.
- Configure the usage source with `codexUsageSource` in **Open Host Settings**; Copilot remains the default.
- Route Copilot usage through the CAPI proxy while launching the OpenAI path without the proxy.
- Publish provider-backed Codex settings through `RootState.config` and `_meta`, with reusable harness settings UI in Customizations.
- Read and write Codex personality and auto-review configuration through the app server's configuration APIs.

## Reviewer Notes

Codex rollout history can contain provider-bound encrypted reasoning content. When switching between Copilot and OpenAI, the VS Code session remains available but the harness creates a fresh Codex app-server thread instead of resuming the incompatible provider thread.

This change intentionally does not add an OpenAI sign-in flow. Users authenticate with Codex separately, then set:

```json
{
  "codexUsageSource": "openai"
}
```

## Testing

- `npm run compile`
- Scoped hygiene on all changed files
- `npm run valid-layers-check`
- Focused Agent Host/Codex tests: 98 passing
- Launch E2E with Copilot: CAPI proxy request returned HTTP 200 and completed the turn
- Launch E2E with OpenAI: direct OpenAI app-server path completed the turn
- Verified no 401, missing provider, `invalid_encrypted_content`, or resume failures

title: Remove archived sessions from user-created groups
body:
Archiving a session now removes it from any user-created group it belongs to, and restoring it does not restore the former group membership. A group whose last member is archived becomes empty and can be deleted. Also adds a hover hint on the empty-group placeholder row explaining how to add sessions.

author: benibenj
review_comments: [{'user': 'Copilot', 'body': 'This cleanup only examines `changed`, so an archived session arriving in `added` keeps its membership. title: Retry transient Agent Host database initialization
body:
This fixes a recovery issue exposed when an Agent Host machine temporarily runs out of disk space.

When the initial per-session SQLite open failed, `SessionDatabase` retained the rejected initialization promise. Long-lived session references would then continue returning the original `SQLITE_CANTOPEN` failure even after the filesystem became writable again.

The initialization promise is now cleared on any setup failure, allowing the next database operation to retry. A regression test covers an initially blocked database path becoming writable.

Validation:
- TypeScript client type-check passed
- Staged-file hygiene passed
- Focused unit test could not run locally because dependency installation is currently blocked by a 404 for the pinned `@vscode/codicons@0.0.46-24` package; CI will run the test

(Written by Copilot)
author: roblourens
review_comments: [{'user': 'Copilot', 'body': 'After `fs.rm(databaseDir)`, the parent directory for `databasePath` no longer exists, so the second `setMetadata` can still fail unless `SessionDatabase` creates parent directories (SQLite itself won’t). To make the test deterministic, recreate `databaseDir` as a directory before the second write (e.g., `await fs.mkdir(databaseDir, { recursive: true })`), or use an explicit permission-based block/unblock on an existing directory.', 'created_at': '2026-07-24T04:20:55+00:00', 'path': 'src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/sessionDatabase.test.ts', 'position': 19}, {'user': 'Copilot', 'body': '`assert.rejects` currently only checks that the call fails, but not that it failed for the intended reason (transient open failure). This can hide regressions where the failure is due to an unrelated issue. Consider asserting on the error shape/message (e.g., matching `SQLITE_CANTOPEN` or the expected errno) so the test clearly validates the retry behavior you’re targeting.', 'created_at': '2026-07-24T04:20:55+00:00', 'path': 'src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/sessionDatabase.test.ts', 'position': 1}, {'user': 'Copilot', 'body': 'Clearing `_dbPromise` for any initialization error can cause repeated reinitialization attempts in tight loops for persistent failures (e.g., corrupted DB schema, invalid SQL, permission issues that won’t resolve), which may add load and noisy logs. If the intent is specifically to recover from transient open/setup failures, consider only clearing `_dbPromise` for those error classes (e.g., `SQLITE_CANTOPEN`/I/O-related errors) or adding a minimal retry backoff / failure throttling to avoid hot-loop retries.', 'created_at': '2026-07-24T04:20:55+00:00', 'path': 'src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/sessionDatabase.ts', 'position': 8}, {'user': 'roblourens', 'body': 'The missing parent directory is intentional: `SessionDatabase._ensureDb()` calls recursive `mkdir` before opening SQLite. The first call fails because that path is a file; after removing it, the retry must create the directory itself. Adding `mkdir` in the test would bypass part of the recovery path being covered. (Written by Copilot)', 'created_at': '2026-07-24T05:05:01+00:00', 'path': 'src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/sessionDatabase.test.ts', 'position': 19}, {'user': 'roblourens', 'body': 'Addressed in 0a4377a5d76: the test now asserts the deterministic `EEXIST` error from the deliberately blocked initialization path and uses initialization rather than open in its name. (Written by Copilot)', 'created_at': '2026-07-24T05:05:01+00:00', 'path': 'src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/sessionDatabase.test.ts', 'position': 1}, {'user': 'roblourens', 'body': 'There is no automatic retry loop here: a retry only occurs when a caller explicitly performs another database operation. Resetting all initialization failures is intentional because transient errors can occur during parent-directory setup, SQLite open, or migrations (including ENOSPC during migration). Caching any rejected initialization promise permanently poisons the long-lived reference. (Written by Copilot)', 'created_at': '2026-07-24T05:05:02+00:00', 'path': 'src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/sessionDatabase.ts', 'position': 8}]

title: agentHost: stabilize resume fallback tests
body:
## Summary

Fixes #327214 and follows up on the flaky test disabled in #327213.

- restore immediate initial session customization discovery
- move Copilot resume-fallback coverage to the deterministic `CopilotSessionLauncher` boundary
- keep watcher-driven refreshes debounced

## Root cause

#325407 intentionally changed the initial discovery call to use a zero delay while keeping the 100 ms debounce for subsequent watcher refreshes. The long-running #325241 branch had started before that change and modified the same constructor. When it later merged `main`, the merge result retained the branch's older call without the zero-delay argument.

That made `_resumeSession` wait on debounced customization discovery. In the failing Windows CI run, this test first passed in 111 ms, then timed out at 2 seconds while the adjacent fallback test took 1.2 seconds, indicating runner load was stretching unrelated timer/filesystem work.

## Test changes

The three fallback tests previously called the full private `CopilotAgent._resumeSession` path. Although they only intended to verify the launcher's resume-error policy, they also exercised authentication, temp-directory creation, customization discovery and watchers, session database setup, agent-session construction, and async shutdown.

The fallback policy is implemented by `CopilotSessionLauncher.launch`, so the tests now invoke that boundary directly with a small fake SDK client:

- a realistic Start Over `-32603` / `no events` error must call `createSession` once
- an unknown `-32603` must call `createSession` once
- a corruption error must propagate and never call `createSession`

The assertions are unchanged in meaning, but the tests no longer depend on timers, filesystem discovery, SQLite, authentication, or agent teardown. Existing `CopilotAgent` tests continue to cover the agent-level resume path, including custom-agent restoration and retry behavior.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client`
- 139 tests across `copilotAgent.test.ts` and `copilotSessionLauncher.test.ts`
- fallback suite passed in 20/20 fresh Electron processes
- changed-file hygiene
- `npm run valid-layers-check`

title: Retire completed non-PTY shell output resources
body:
Resolves: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/327178
Follow-up to: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/327067

- Add idempotent retirement for completed non-PTY shell output resources, removing both the host resource and its tracked stream.
- Publish the final `ChatToolCallComplete` result before retiring the live output resource so completed rendering has an authoritative static result.
- Retire only when both an exit code and preview are available; an empty preview still counts as authoritative.
- Keep background and no-preview output streams session-owned until normal session disposal.

title: Reuse terminals when replacing new session drafts
body:
Resolves: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/327169

- Add `onDidReplaceNewDraftSession` for the workspace New Session → New Session lifecycle, distinct from draft graduation.
- Fire the event before publishing the replacement draft so terminal ownership moves before eager terminal creation.
- Transfer existing terminals when both drafts use the same CWD and Agent Host backend, preserving the process and scrollback.
- Rehome incompatible terminals as standalone terminals, excluding them from later session matching and visibility management.
- Dispose terminals that finish creating after their draft was replaced, before they can be activated or tracked.
- Document draft replacement ordering and terminal ownership in the Sessions specification.
- Cover repeated Agent Host draft replacement, multiple tracked terminals, compatibility boundaries, standalone ownership, and asynchronous creation races.

- The replacement event shape and draft-graduation distinction come from [`ISessionsManagementService.onDidReplaceSession`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/a71d15db91072496a839f1400321b35d9f301c60/src/vs/sessions/services/sessions/common/sessionsManagement.ts#L285-L294).

title: Incrementally refine dictation transcripts
body:
Fixes #327222
Fixes #327219

## Summary

- periodically refine stable portions of the live dictation transcript instead of waiting until recording stops
- send at most 800 trailing characters per incremental request, with a five-second minimum interval
- preserve the previously refined display prefix while keeping the raw ASR transcript untouched for final cleanup and fallback
- cancel stale or overlapping refinement requests when dictation stops, is cancelled, or speech recognition revises the processed prefix
- reject cleanup output that adds or rewrites dictated words, preventing requests from being followed as instructions or turned into generated HTML/code
- ask post-processing to format dictated sequences as Markdown bullet or numbered lists

## How incremental cleanup works

While the user dictates, VS Code periodically sends a stable portion of the recent transcript to the cleanup model. During active transcription it leaves the newest 20 characters untouched because speech recognition may still revise them; after one second without an update, the complete live tail is considered stable, including short dictation. Cleaned text appears while recording continues. If speech recognition revises processed words, stale cleanup is cancelled and retried. When recording stops, the complete raw transcript receives the existing authoritative final cleanup pass.

Both incremental and final cleanup are controlled by `dictation.experimental.llmCleanup`. Disabling the setting turns off both behaviors.

The final cleanup retains its timeout, cancellation, length limit, output-faithfulness validation, and raw-transcript fallback behavior.

title: Voice: don't auto-send the turn by default when hands-free is disabled
body:
Fixes #327217

## What

When hands-free mode (`agents.voice.handsFree`) is **disabled**, voice mode no longer auto-sends the turn by default. Previously the turn ended automatically on trailing silence (`agents.voice.turn.silenceMs`, default `800`) and on a stop phrase (`agents.voice.turn.stopPhrases`, default `['send it']`) regardless of the hands-free setting, which is surprising for users who opt out of the automatic back-and-forth loop.

## How

In `voiceClientService._getTurnConfig()`:
- Read `agents.voice.handsFree`.
- When hands-free is disabled, suppress trailing-silence ending unless `agents.voice.turn.silenceMs` is **explicitly** configured, and suppress stop-phrase ending unless `agents.voice.turn.stopPhrases` is explicitly configured (via `IConfigurationService.inspect()`).
- Users who explicitly set either setting keep that behavior; the derived `auto_end_mode` becomes `off` only when nothing opts in.

Also:
- Re-send the turn config to the backend when `agents.voice.handsFree` changes (previously only silence/phrase changes triggered a resend).
- Update the setting descriptions for `agents.voice.turn.silenceMs`, `agents.voice.turn.stopPhrases`, and `agents.voice.handsFree` to document this.

## Notes

- No behavior change when hands-free is enabled (the default), or when the turn settings are explicitly configured.
- Draft.

title: Experimental: clean up dictation transcript with a language model
body:
Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/327205
Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/327204

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6d0d5525-9840-4104-910a-4d66d051a9db

## Clean up dictation transcript with a language model

Our built-in on-device dictation (streaming Nemotron ASR via Foundry Local) emits lowercase, largely unpunctuated text and transcribes filler words verbatim, so dictated input reads as one long run-on. The underlying model and the Foundry SDK expose no punctuation option, so this runs the final transcript through a small language model to restore formatting.

### How it works
- Setting **`dictation.experimental.llmCleanup`** (on by default, experimental).
- After the raw transcript is produced, `ChatSpeechToTextService.stopAndTranscribe()` sends it once to `copilot-utility-small` (via `ILanguageModelsService`) with a strict "only fix punctuation, casing, spacing, and paragraphs; preserve wording; drop fillers/false starts; never answer" prompt, then returns the cleaned text.
- Robust and non-blocking:
  - Owns a per-cleanup `CancellationTokenSource` with a 10s deadline; cancelled from `cancel()`. If the session is aborted mid-cleanup, `stopAndTranscribe()` bails without touching shared state, so it can never get stuck in `Transcribing` or tear down a newly started session.
  - Transcripts over the 4000-char cap skip cleanup and return raw (no truncation).
  - The response stream is consumed with strict error propagation and `await response.result`, so only a complete response can replace the transcript — a mid-stream failure falls back to the raw transcript.
  - `finalizeMs` telemetry is measured after cleanup so it reflects model latency.

### Gating
Programmatically gated on Copilot: with AI features disabled, `selectLanguageModels` returns none and cleanup is skipped, falling back to the raw transcript.

review_comments: [{'user': 'Copilot', 'body': 'The cleanup request is passed `CancellationToken.None`, so `cancel()` cannot stop it and there is no deadline. In the terminal path, an abort calls `service.cancel()` and makes the service idle while this await is still pending; a new recording can then start, and when this old request completes it continues to `_teardown()` and stops the new recording. A stalled provider also leaves dictation in `Transcribing` indefinitely. Please own a per-cleanup cancellation source, cancel it from the service lifecycle, impose a bounded timeout, and stop the old finalization path after cancellation.', 'created_at': '2026-07-23T22:10:59+00:00', 'path': 'src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/speechToText/chatSpeechToTextService.ts', 'position': 1}, {'user': 'Copilot', 'body': 'This records `finalizeMs` before the newly added cleanup await, although the telemetry contract defines it as the time until the final transcript resolves. Every successful cleanup therefore hides its network/model latency—the main operational cost of this experiment. Move the assignment after cleanup so the metric reflects the transcript returned to the caller.', 'created_at': '2026-07-23T22:10:59+00:00', 'path': 'src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/speechToText/chatSpeechToTextService.ts', 'position': 1}, {'user': 'Copilot', 'body': 'For transcripts longer than 4,000 characters, only the prefix is sent but the returned prefix later replaces the entire transcript. This silently deletes everything after character 4,000, contradicting the raw-transcript fallback guarantee. ['Experimental: clean up dictation transcript with a language model

Add an opt-in `dictation.experimental.llmCleanup` setting that passes the final
on-device dictation transcript through a small utility language model
(copilot-utility-small, in the spirit of gpt-4o-mini) to restore punctuation,
capitalization, and paragraph breaks that the streaming ASR model omits, and to
drop filler words. Runs once in stopAndTranscribe() after the raw transcript is
produced; falls back to the raw transcript when no model is available (e.g. AI
features disabled) or the request fails. Off by default.

- Own a per-cleanup CancellationTokenSource with a 10s deadline; cancel it from

  cleanup ran, so a stalled/aborted request can't leave dictation stuck in
  Transcribing or tear down a newly started session.

- Skip cleanup for transcripts over the char cap instead of truncating them,
  preserving the raw-transcript fallback guarantee.
- Consume the response stream with strict error propagation and await
  response.result, so only a complete response can replace the transcript.
- Clarify the prompt: preserve wording, with an explicit exception for filler

- bind the automation composer to the selected provider’s concrete model target instead of its logical session type
- canonicalize legacy matching Agent Host model identifiers before readiness resolution

Automations targeting Local Agent Host persisted extension-backed identifiers such as `copilotcli/gpt-5.6-sol`, while the selected provider advertises `agent-host-copilotcli:gpt-5.6-sol`. title: Improve built-in dictation by filtering filler words
body:
Fixes #327205

## Improve built-in dictation punctuation and remove filler words

Our on-device dictation (streaming Nemotron ASR via Foundry Local) emits lowercase, largely unpunctuated per-segment text, and transcribes speech disfluencies verbatim. The result reads as one long lowercase run-on sentence full of "um" and "uh". 

### Changes
- **Filler suppression**: strip standalone filler tokens (`um`/`umm`, `uh`/`uhh`, `uhm`, `er`/`erm`, `hm`/`hmm`) and their lengthened variants per segment, tidy leftover spacing, and drop segments that were only filler. Word boundaries keep real words like "huh", "duh", "summon" intact.

Both apply to live finalized updates and the final `stop()` transcript. Always on, since the raw output is objectively worse. The interim (shimmering) partial tail is left raw and re-normalizes when it finalizes.

### Tests
Added `localTranscriptionService.test.ts` covering run-on splitting, short-pause joins, no double-punctuation, "i" → "I", null-timing fallback, filler stripping/variants, filler-only segments, and preservation of filler-like real words.

For example, `um, hello` becomes `, hello`, while a filler-only `um.` becomes `.` and is therefore not dropped. Make this cleanup punctuation-aware and cover leading, trailing, and punctuated filler cases.

This issue also appears in the following locations of the same file:

commit_messages:
['Auto-punctuate built-in dictation to fix run-on sentences

The on-device streaming ASR model (nemotron-speech-streaming-en-0.6b via
Foundry Local) emits lowercase, largely unpunctuated per-segment text, and
the Foundry SDK exposes no punctuation/format option. TranscriptAccumulator
previously joined segments with spaces only, producing one long lowercase
run-on sentence.

Post-process the finalized transcript in getText(): insert a sentence break
when a deliberate pause (>= 0.7s, from segment start/end timing) separates two
unterminated segments, and capitalize sentence starts plus the standalone
pronoun "i". Falls back to the prior space-join when segment timing is
unavailable. This covers both live finalized updates and the final stop()
transcript. Always on, since the raw output is objectively worse.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

so dictated text is cluttered with "um", "uh", "erm", etc. Strip standalone
filler tokens (including lengthened variants like "umm"/"uhh") per segment in
TranscriptAccumulator.getText() before sentence assembly, tidy the leftover
whitespace/punctuation spacing, and drop any segment that was only filler.
Word boundaries keep real words that merely contain those letters ("huh",
"duh", "summon") intact.

body:
Wrap provider-advertised Agent Host model IDs in `TelemetryTrustedValue` so known model IDs are not path-redacted. BYOK models are reported as `byokModel`, and selections absent from the provider catalog are reported as `unknown`.

Adds turn telemetry coverage for trusted, BYOK, and unknown model selections.

(Written by Copilot)

review_comments: [{'user': 'Copilot', 'body': "As written, any callsite that passes `model` but leaves `modelTelemetryKind` undefined will force the emitted `model` to `'unknown'`. This makes the new `modelTelemetryKind` effectively mandatory (despite the type allowing `undefined`) and risks unintended behavior if any caller wasn’t updated. Consider making the mapping resilient: if `modelTelemetryKind` is `undefined`, keep `report.model` as-is (preserving existing semantics), and only apply trusted/BYOK/unknown mapping when an explicit kind is provided.", 'created_at': '2026-07-23T17:46:31+00:00', 'path': 'src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentHostTelemetryReporter.ts', 'position': 50}, {'user': 'Copilot', 'body': "This treats a special selection like `modelId === 'auto'` as `'unknown'` (since it won’t usually exist in the provider’s model catalog). title: fix: guard undefined stdio command in MCP server identity (fixes #327148)
body:
### Summary `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'includes')` thrown from `McpServer._hasUnresolvedVariables` (`src/vs/workbench/contrib/mcp/common/mcpServer.ts:745`). The MCP policy-governance layer builds an `IMcpServerIdentity` from a stdio launch via `_identityFromLaunch` as `command: [launch.command, ...launch.args]`. Although `McpServerLaunch.Stdio.command` is typed `string`, discovery/config producers assign it directly from untrusted configuration (e.g. `pluginMcpDiscovery._toLaunch` and `nativeMcpDiscoveryAdapters` use `command: config.command` / `command: server.command`). When a user's stdio MCP entry omits `command`, that value is `undefined`, so the produced `identity.command` array contains an `undefined` element — violating `IMcpServerIdentity.command: readonly string[]`. The new policy check `_hasUnresolvedVariables` then calls `arg.includes(...)` on that `undefined` element and throws inside the reactive `_policyBlock` autorun during `McpService.updateCollectedServers`. ### Notes
- Default remains `false`; this only affects discoverability, not behavior.

title: Add dictation backend selection; support for using MAI; rename dictation settings
body:
## Dictation backend selection + settings cleanup

Adds a cloud dictation backend option and regroups the dictation settings under a generic `dictation.*` namespace, since these settings govern dictation across chat, editor, and terminal — not just chat.

### Settings

| Old | New | Change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `chat.speechToText.model` | `dictation.model` | Renamed; adds a cloud **`mai`** option alongside the on-device Nemotron model. |
| `chat.speechToText.enabled` | `dictation.enabled` | Renamed to a generic dictation kill-switch. |
| `chat.speechToText.mode` | _(removed)_ | The shortcut now always uses the former `auto` behavior: tap toggles, hold is push-to-talk. |

Settings migrations map any stored `chat.speechToText.*` values (including legacy on-device model ids) to the new keys, preserving an already-configured destination value (e.g. after settings sync) and clearing the removed `mode` key.

### Backends

- **`nemotron-speech-streaming-en-0.6b`** (default): on-device, via `ILocalTranscriptionService` (Foundry Local). Offline; no audio leaves the device.
- **`mai`**: cloud, via `IVoiceClientService` — the same voice service Voice Mode uses. Streams PCM16 over the voice websocket (PTT), authenticated with the GitHub token. Requires network + sign-in.

Selecting `mai` routes dictation start/stop/audio through the voice client instead of the local transcription service; nemo remains the default.

**Shared-connection safety** (the voice socket is a single connection shared with Voice Mode):
- Refuses to start when the socket is already connected, and only disconnects a connection this dictation established — so dictation and Voice Mode can't tear down each other's session.
- Requires GitHub sign-in (fails with an actionable message) before connecting rather than opening an unauthenticated socket.
- Filters transcription events by `turnId` and drops non-increasing `revision`s, so a late/other-turn event can't corrupt the transcript or resolve the final waiter early.
- Subscribes to `onFatalDisconnect` (terminal close codes 4001/4008/4029, e.g. another window took over) and fails/tears down the session — closing the mic — with a user-facing message.

### Telemetry (backend comparison)

The goal is to A/B compare the two backends, so dictation emits two events sliced by `backend` (`nemo` / `mai`) and `surface` (chat / editor / terminal).

**`chatSpeechToText.session`** — usage, reliability, and latency:
- `timeToFirstTranscriptMs` — first streamed audio → first transcript; isolates backend transcription latency (excludes mic acquisition + model download).
- `finalizeMs` — stop → final transcript; the post-stop wait.
- `partialUpdates` — count of interim (non-final) updates; a churn/stability proxy.
- plus existing `outcome`, `segments`, `transcriptLength`, `errorCode`.

**`chatSpeechToText.accuracy`** — a ground-truth-free accuracy proxy: how much the user edits dictated text before sending it. After a dictation finalizes, the dictated span is followed with a tracked decoration; the diff is measured at the **actual submit** (a `notifyDictationSubmitted` hook in the chat input part and the Agents composer send path, before the editor clears), falling back to clear/teardown otherwise:
- `dictatedLength`, `editDistance` (Levenshtein), `editRate` (`editDistance/dictatedLength`, capped at 1; lower is more accurate), `edited`, and `submitted` (whether an actual send fired vs. a clear/teardown).

Only aggregate character metrics are logged — never any transcript text. Edits typed at the span's edges are excluded so unrelated appended text isn't counted.

Examples (`editRate` = `editDistance / dictatedLength`, capped at 1):

| Scenario | dictated → submitted | editDistance | editRate | edited |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Clean, sent as-is | `add a retry to the upload handler` → _(same)_ | 0 | 0.00 | false |
| One misheard word fixed | `fix the of by one error…` → `fix the off by one error…` | 1 | 0.03 | true |
| Mostly rewritten | `um open the setting is file` → `refactor the parser` | 22 | 0.82 | true |

Across many sessions, a better backend shows more `edited=false` and lower `editRate` on the rest; `submitted=true` rows are the trustworthy signal.

### Notes

- Whether the MAI backend requires an explicit `sendStartSession` before PTT transcription still needs verification against a live backend; draft until validated end-to-end.

['Add dictation backend selection; rename dictation settings

Let users choose which backend transcribes dictation audio, and regroup
the dictation settings under a generic `dictation.*` namespace since they
govern dictation across chat, editor, and terminal.

- `dictation.model` (was `chat.speechToText.model`): now includes a
  cloud `mai` option that reuses the Voice Mode voice service, alongside
  the on-device Nemotron model. Selecting `mai` routes dictation through
  IVoiceClientService (PTT stream) instead of ILocalTranscriptionService.
- `dictation.enabled` (was `chat.speechToText.enabled`): generic
  dictation kill-switch.
- Removed `chat.speechToText.mode`; the shortcut now always uses the
  former `auto` behavior (tap toggles, hold is push-to-talk).
- Added settings migrations from the old `chat.speechToText.*` keys.
- Added backend-comparison telemetry (backend slicer, partialUpdates,
  timeToFirstTranscriptMs, finalizeMs) to compare model quality/latency.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
Copilot-Session: da6e59a8-07f0-468f-a500-4f96b981ba51', "Add post-dictation edit-distance accuracy telemetry

Measure how much of each dictated transcript the user edits before the
text leaves the input, as a ground-truth-free accuracy proxy to compare
the on-device and cloud backends.

- Track the dictated span with a decoration after a session finalizes, so
  it stays aligned as the user edits around it (edits at its edges are
  excluded so unrelated appended text isn't counted).
- When the text leaves the input (submit clears the editor, or the editor
  is disposed), compute the Levenshtein distance between what was dictated
  and what was submitted and emit `chatSpeechToText.accuracy` with
  backend/surface slicers plus dictatedLength, editDistance, editRate, and
  edited. Only aggregate character metrics are logged; no transcript text.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
Copilot-Session: da6e59a8-07f0-468f-a500-4f96b981ba51", 'Address review feedback; use precise submit signal for accuracy

Accuracy telemetry:
- Measure edit distance at the actual input submit via a new
  notifyDictationSubmitted() hook wired into the chat input part and the
  Agents composer send path, before the editor is cleared. The
  clear-to-empty / editor-dispose heuristics remain as fallbacks, and a
  `submitted` flag records which path fired.

MAI (cloud) backend hardening:
- Refuse to start when the shared voice socket is already connected, and
  only disconnect a connection this dictation established, so dictation
  and Voice Mode can't tear down each other's session.
- Require a GitHub sign-in (fail with an actionable message) before
  connecting instead of opening an unauthenticated socket.
- Filter transcription events by turnId and drop non-increasing revisions
  so a late/other-turn event can't corrupt the transcript or resolve the
  final waiter early.
- Subscribe to onFatalDisconnect and fail/tear down the session (closing
  the mic) with a user-facing message on a terminal close.

Settings:
- Only count non-final updates in the partialUpdates metric.
- Localize the dictation.model enum item labels.
- Preserve an explicitly configured destination in the model/enabled
  migrations (don't clobber synced values) and migrate the removed
  chat.speechToText.mode key away.
- Recompute Agents-composer mic visibility on dictation.model changes too.
- Drop "on-device" from dictation accessibility-help copy since the cloud
  backend streams audio off-device.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
Copilot-Session: da6e59a8-07f0-468f-a500-4f96b981ba51', "Open backend session before streaming MAI dictation audio

The MAI (cloud) dictation path connected the shared voice websocket and
sent ptt_start/audio without first opening a session, so the backend
silently dropped all audio: no transcription, no error. Send start_session
with a minimal session-less context and wait for the backend's
onSessionInit ack (with a timeout fallback) before ptt_start.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
Copilot-Session: da6e59a8-07f0-468f-a500-4f96b981ba51", 'Fix MAI dictation dropping phrases and leaking prior transcript

Reusing the conversational voice socket for dictation applied the default
turn config (auto_end_mode: vad, 800ms silence), so the backend ended the
turn on the first pause between phrases: everything after the first phrase
landed in a new turn and was dropped, and the auto-ended transcript could
resurface on the next session. Open the dictation turn with auto-end off
and ASR ungated so one continuous turn spans the whole recording. Also
reset transcript state on start and add trace logging for the MAI path.
