title: Style overrides: Consolidate CSS selectors and unify surface color tokens
body:
This pull request introduces a new set of generic `surface.*` theme tokens for container surfaces (such as floating panels), updates the modern workbench layout to use these tokens instead of the agent-specific ones, and refactors related CSS for better maintainability and consistency. Additionally, it standardizes font and spacing variable usage by replacing agent-specific variables with the default ones, and cleans up some CSS selectors for improved specificity and maintainability.

**Theme tokens and styling updates:**

* Added new `surface.background`, `surface.foreground`, and `surface.border` theme tokens in `src/vs/workbench/common/theme.ts`, with appropriate defaults and documentation for use with generic container "cards".
* Updated dark and light theme JSON files to define values for the new `surface.*` tokens, mirroring the previous `agentsPanel.*` values for consistency [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-ed93cc8becd22ae30b99dc456a0aaa6b779e7b4b542d4bee95cf759ee517b3c9R287-R289) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-87dd8146fec1e0d71789bc1cb459b84af52652eab3e70b77227bbcdeaca73301R295-R297).
* Registered the new `surface.*` tokens in the stylelint variables list for editor integration and linting.

**CSS refactoring and variable standardization:**

* Updated all relevant CSS in `floatingPanels.css`, `editorBorder.css`, and related files to use the new `surface.*` tokens instead of `agentsPanel.*`, ensuring that floating panels and cards share a consistent look and are easily themeable [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-96cb2d8573ce4ce529610b032f2044a61b322357bff73870ab0196ceec6f17b3L16-R17) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-96cb2d8573ce4ce529610b032f2044a61b322357bff73870ab0196ceec6f17b3L25-R38) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-73774406b10b7aea37c99d6e66f2a4e427301ff26607dc69e475c731a1618b05L45-R67).
* Replaced agent-specific font and size variables (e.g., `--vscode-agents-fontWeight-semiBold`, `--vscode-agents-fontSize-label2`) with the default `--vscode-fontWeight-semiBold` and `--vscode-fontSize-label2` throughout style override CSS files for better maintainability and to avoid duplication [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-c718522311de21a7658a924bbd223350855e39acf9ddd9e1c4eaffa8f76a34dbL313-R313) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-949ec94438c04f89d57f6ad30dfdd93a1ea7e72c5d2d51b032ed5e6c16d0901fL148-R148) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-949ec94438c04f89d57f6ad30dfdd93a1ea7e72c5d2d51b032ed5e6c16d0901fL202-R202) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-c5122c2b03b035b623843dbb023ad264a4b1b7da4ad722e800292178087267e5L95-R95) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-915cccdddaa0b83d00bb30841bbd79387a84f1f638b32f49633b200309e03024L35-R35) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-915cccdddaa0b83d00bb30841bbd79387a84f1f638b32f49633b200309e03024L227-R224) [[7]](diffhunk://#diff-915cccdddaa0b83d00bb30841bbd79387a84f1f638b32f49633b200309e03024L271-R275) [[8]](diffhunk://#diff-915cccdddaa0b83d00bb30841bbd79387a84f1f638b32f49633b200309e03024L305-R302) [[9]](diffhunk://#diff-915cccdddaa0b83d00bb30841bbd79387a84f1f638b32f49633b200309e03024L347-R344).

**CSS selector improvements:**

* Simplified and unified CSS selectors in `keyboardFocusOnly.css` using the `:is()` pseudo-class for better specificity and maintainability [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-ac3294ab4f135eb1db1a6f725ae25fbfdedc46311de22631c313542d04c8f47cL30-R30) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-ac3294ab4f135eb1db1a6f725ae25fbfdedc46311de22631c313542d04c8f47cL43-R42).

**Minor layout and cleanup:**

* Moved the `.tab.sticky-compact` width rules to a more appropriate location in the CSS for clarity [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-915cccdddaa0b83d00bb30841bbd79387a84f1f638b32f49633b200309e03024R45-R48) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-915cccdddaa0b83d00bb30841bbd79387a84f1f638b32f49633b200309e03024L85-L91).

These changes improve the theming flexibility of the workbench, make the codebase easier to maintain, and ensure a more consistent visual appearance across different UI surfaces.

title: Restore last-used agent-host model instead of falling back to Auto
body:
## Summary

Agent-host chat sessions (e.g. **Copilot CLI**) publish their model list **asynchronously**, only after the agent host process connects. During that cold-start window, VS Code's model-restore logic treated a remembered/last-used model that wasn't in the (still-empty) pool as **conclusively unavailable** and reset the model picker to **Auto**, instead of waiting for the pool to load.

The result: after selecting a specific model (e.g. `GPT-5.6`) and reopening VS Code / a session / a different repo, the model picker showed **Auto** instead of the model you last used.

## Root cause

`isLanguageModelVendorAbsenceConclusive` only granted the built-in **Copilot** vendor a "an empty result during startup is transient" grace. Agent-host vendors (`agent-host-*` local, `remote-*` remote) load their models asynchronously too, but an empty resolution was treated as **final** → the remembered model resolved as `unavailable` → the restore gave up and fell back to Auto.

Because this defect is at the resolution layer, it leaked into **every** restore surface (a new editor, the sidebar chat view, and reopened existing sessions).

**Fix:** give agent-host vendors the same transient grace as Copilot, so an absent model on a still-empty pool resolves as `pending` (wait) rather than `unavailable` (give up):

```ts
return hasLiveModels || (hasResolved && vendor !== COPILOT_VENDOR_ID && !isAgentHostVendor(vendor));
```

This fixes all surfaces at once and naturally survives the transient empty resolutions emitted before the real models arrive (resolution stays `pending` until the pool loads). Two supporting hardening changes are included (see **Changes**).

## Issues fixed — with step-by-step repro

> These are agent-host sessions (Copilot CLI). The bug reproduces on a **cold start** — i.e. the first open before the agent-host model list has been fetched/cached. Reproducing reliably may require selecting a **non-Auto** model, sending a message, and fully **restarting** VS Code.

### Issue 1 — Reopening an existing session restores as Auto
1. Open folder **A** in VS Code.
2. Open a new chat editor for an agent-host session (Copilot CLI).
3. Select a specific model (e.g. **GPT-5.6**), send a message, and wait for completion.
4. **Fully exit** VS Code.
5. Start VS Code again in the **same** folder **A** — the previous session is restored automatically.
6. ❌ **Before:** the restored session's model shows **Auto**.
   ✅ **After:** the restored session shows the model you used (**GPT-5.6**).

### Issue 2 — Sidebar chat view opens on Auto after switching repos
1. Open folder **A**, select a model (e.g. **GPT-5.6**) in an agent-host session, send a message, wait for completion.
2. **Fully exit** VS Code.
3. Open VS Code in a **different** folder **B**.
4. Open a **new chat editor** — the model is correctly your last-used model.
5. Open the **Chat panel in the sidebar** (Copilot CLI).
6. ❌ **Before:** the sidebar chat shows **Auto** (even though the editor showed the right model).
   ✅ **After:** the sidebar chat shows your last-used model.

### Issue 3 — New chat editor in a different repo opens on Auto
1. Open folder **A**, select a model (e.g. **GPT-5.6 Terra**) in an agent-host session, send a message, wait for completion.
2. **Fully exit** VS Code.
3. Open VS Code in a **different** folder **B**.
4. Open a new chat editor for the agent-host session.
5. ❌ **Before (cold pool):** the model briefly/persistently shows **Auto**.
   ✅ **After:** the model shows your last-used model once the agent-host models load.

In all three cases the user's selection *was* saved correctly (in the per-session-type storage bucket); the bug was purely on the **restore/read** side — the picker gave up on the remembered model before the agent-host pool finished loading.

## Changes

- **`common/languageModels.ts`** — the root fix. Add `isAgentHostVendor(...)` (using platform-layer prefix helpers to avoid an import cycle) and exclude agent-host vendors from "conclusive absence", mirroring the existing Copilot behavior. This also lets `mergeModelsWithCache` keep cached agent-host models during the load window (same as Copilot).
- **`common/chatService/chatServiceImpl.ts`** — `loadRemoteSession` no longer drops the session's known model to `undefined` when the live lookup is cold; it carries the saved model (with metadata) into the restored input state, including through a transferred draft (new small helper `backfillRestoredModel`).
- **`browser/widget/input/chatInputModelSelectionController.ts`** — `syncFromConversationState` keeps waiting through transient empty agent-host resolutions and only falls back once the session-type pool has actually loaded without the model.

## Tests

New regression tests, **verified to fail if the root fix is reverted**:

- `modelSelection.test.ts` — `treats a resolved-but-empty agent-host vendor as still loading (pending)` (covers local + remote; and `unavailable` once the pool loads without the model).
- `chatModelSelectionModel.test.ts` — `initialize waits for a resolved-but-empty agent-host pool and restores the remembered model` (drives the restore through the real catalog resolver; asserts it waits through an intermediate empty event and applies the model on load) and `waits through a resolved-but-empty session pool and applies the restored model when it loads`.
- `chatService.test.ts` — `backfillRestoredModel` suite for the `loadRemoteSession` carry-over.

I temporarily reverted the root-fix clause and confirmed both new agent-host tests fail (`2 failing, 0 passing`), then restored it.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client` ✅
- `npm run valid-layers-check` ✅ (new platform→chat import verified)
- ESLint on changed files ✅
- Suites: `ModelSelection` (55), `ChatModelSelectionModel` (19), `ChatInputModelUtils` (136, incl. cache — no regression), `backfillRestored`/`chatService` backfill (8) ✅

This exception makes `mergeModelsWithCache` retain cached agent-host entries indefinitely whenever the live list is empty, so the input no longer reaches its “No models available”/send-blocked state and can offer a removed or unentitled model. Please add an explicit agent-host readiness signal, or separate restore resolution from cache-retention policy, so the startup grace ends when an empty list is authoritative.', 'created_at': '2026-07-22T09:51:25+00:00', 'path': 'src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/languageModels.ts', 'position': 1}, {'user': 'Copilot', 'body': 'An empty targeted pool is not necessarily still loading. commit_messages:
['fix(chat): restore last-used agent-host model instead of falling back to Auto

Agent-host chat sessions (e.g. Copilot CLI) publish their model list
asynchronously after the agent host connects. During that cold-start
window the model-restore logic treated an absent remembered/session
model as conclusively unavailable and reset the picker to "Auto" instead
of waiting for the pool to load. This affected new chat editors, the
sidebar chat view, and reopened existing sessions.

Root fix: give agent-host vendors the same "empty results are transient"
grace already applied to Copilot in isLanguageModelVendorAbsenceConclusive,
so a remembered/restored model resolves as `pending` (wait) rather than
`unavailable` (give up) while the agent-host model pool is still loading.
This fixes every restore surface at once (initialize, conversation-restore
and their model-change waiters) and naturally survives the transient empty
resolutions emitted before the real models arrive.

Additional hardening:
- loadRemoteSession: carry the session's known model (with metadata) into
  the restored input state when the live lookup is cold, including through
  a transferred draft, instead of dropping it to undefined.
- syncFromConversationState: keep waiting through transient empty
  agent-host resolutions; only fall back once the pool has loaded without
  the model.

Adds regression tests (verified to fail if the root fix is reverted).

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>', 'address review: scope agent-host grace to resolution; revert redundant wait

Addresses two review comments on #326938:

- Relocate the agent-host "empty is transient" grace out of the shared
  isLanguageModelVendorAbsenceConclusive (reverted to original) into
  resolveModelIdentifierFromCatalog, so it applies to model-restore
  resolution only and no longer relaxes cache-retention
  (mergeModelsWithCache) or send-availability. A resolved-empty agent-host
  vendor's cache is evicted again (authoritative), so stale/removed models
  aren't offered. The grace is guarded so it only softens the empty-pool
  case; once the vendor has live models an absent model stays conclusive.

- Revert the syncFromConversationState wait change: with the resolution
  grace, agent-host cold-empty already resolves as `pending`, so the extra
  `|| !hasModelsTargetingSession(...)` branch was redundant and would arm a
  never-firing wait for a non-agent-host contributed session whose provider
  resolved to an authoritatively-empty pool (fallback would never run).

Tests: resolution/restore tests now route through the real catalog resolver
and are verified to fail if the grace is removed; a new mergeModelsWithCache
test locks in that a resolved-empty agent-host cache is evicted.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>', "review: reuse canonical isAgentHostTarget instead of a bespoke helper

Replace the local isAgentHostVendor helper (in languageModels.ts) with the
existing isAgentHostTarget from chatSessionsService.ts, used directly in
resolveModelIdentifierFromCatalog. The agent-host model vendor id equals the
session type, so isAgentHostTarget classifies it correctly.

This reverts languageModels.ts back to its original form (the PR no longer
touches it) and avoids duplicating agent-host prefix detection. No import
cycle: modelSelection.ts is only consumed by browser-layer input files, so it
is unreachable from chatSessionsService's common-only dependency graph, and
isAgentHostTarget is a runtime function (not a load-time constant).

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>"]

title: Preserve agent host terminal stream order for command output
body:
Follow-up to: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/325110

- Flush pending `terminal/data` before dispatching the next OSC 633 event so AHP actions preserve the PTY stream order.
- Keep command output between `terminal/commandExecuted` and `terminal/commandFinished`, as required by the AHP terminal contract and matching workbench/xterm shell integration.
- Prevent fast commands whose output and finish marker arrive in one PTY read from completing before live subscribers receive their output. Otherwise, output can become unclassified, command objects can report empty output, and executed/end marks can bracket an empty range.
- Keep ordinary output chunks batched into one `terminal/data` action without changing the protocol schema or version.
- Add coverage for server action ordering, client-state output attribution, and workbench AHP command output.

-----------------------------------------
Inspirations from:

- The ordering requirement comes directly from the [`TerminalCommandExecutedAction` and `TerminalCommandFinishedAction` AHP contract](https://github.com/microsoft/agent-host-protocol/blob/0960c7e1b74860bb055617839aa49ff976b5c39d/types/channels-terminal/actions.ts#L153-L182), which defines intervening `terminal/data` actions as the command's complete output.
- Workbench command detection models the lifecycle as command executed → terminal output → command finished in [`printStandardCommand`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/65f89ec8b234ea8e03a837302bfee2ecca8074c3/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/test/browser/capabilities/commandDetectionCapability.test.ts#L47-L58). Xterm routes OSC 633 `C` and `D` markers inline through [`ShellIntegrationAddon`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/65f89ec8b234ea8e03a837302bfee2ecca8074c3/src/vs/platform/terminal/common/xterm/shellIntegrationAddon.ts#L473-L510), and [`TerminalCommand.getOutput`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/65f89ec8b234ea8e03a837302bfee2ecca8074c3/src/vs/platform/terminal/common/capabilities/commandDetection/terminalCommand.ts#L123-L154) reads the output bounded by the executed and finished markers.
- When that order is not preserved, the [`terminalReducer`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/65f89ec8b234ea8e03a837302bfee2ecca8074c3/src/vs/platform/agentHost/common/state/protocol/channels-terminal/reducer.ts#L17-L87) places data received after completion into unclassified content, while [`AhpTerminalCommandSource`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/65f89ec8b234ea8e03a837302bfee2ecca8074c3/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/browser/ahpTerminalCommandSource.ts#L189-L257) only appends streamed data while the command is executing.

title: sessions: add a Quick Pick entry point for folder selection in new session
body:
## What changed

Adds a native `IQuickInputService` Quick Pick as an additional entry point for picking the target folder when starting a new session in the Agents Window, alongside the existing `WorkspacePicker` dropdown.

- New command `workbench.action.sessions.newSession.pickFolderQuickPick` ("New Session in Folder...") - discoverable via the Command Palette and bound to `Cmd+O` while the Agents Window is focused. The keybinding uses a higher weight than the desktop Open File/Folder actions so it wins on `Cmd+O` conflicts, without disabling those actions anywhere else.
- Lists recently used folders (own history + VS Code's own recents, deduplicated) followed by an always-present "Browse..." entry that opens the native folder dialog.
- Extracted `ISessionsRecentWorkspacesService`, the single source of truth for the sessions' own recently-used workspace folders, shared by the new Quick Pick and the existing `WorkspacePicker` dropdown (and its `WebWorkspacePicker`/`AutomationsWorkspacePicker` variants) so all folder-selection surfaces always agree on the same recent-folder list.
- Fixed `NewChatWidget` to keep the `WorkspacePicker` dropdown's displayed selection in sync when the active session's workspace changes externally (e.g. via the new Quick Pick command while the composer is already showing) - previously it kept showing the stale folder.

## Why

The Agents Window new-session view only had a custom `ActionWidget`-based dropdown for folder selection. This adds a lighter-weight, keyboard-first Quick Pick alternative without touching the existing dropdown's behavior.

## Notes for reviewers

- `sessionsProvidersService.ts` is untouched (no diff) - workspace resolution stays local to the picker and to the recent-workspaces service (which resolves entries internally before returning them), keeping `ISessionsProvidersService`'s surface unchanged.
- No default keybinding conflicts are introduced outside the Agents Window; `Cmd+O` elsewhere in VS Code is unaffected.

title: agentHost: Respect disabled AI features
body:
Fixes #326634

## Summary
- include `chat.disableAIFeatures` in the central Agent Host startup enablement decision
- preserve the existing eager, fixed-at-startup enablement lifecycle
- prevent Agent Host process startup and hide dependent Agent Host features after a fresh restart when AI features are disabled
- add regression coverage for the enablement result and context key

## Validation
- `npm run precommit`
- Electron unit tests: AgentHostEnablementService
- browser unit tests: AgentHostEnablementService
- direct A/B isolated fresh launches with workspace-scoped `.vscode/settings.json` while the service remained Eager:
  - `chat.disableAIFeatures: true` → Agent Host process not spawned
  - `chat.disableAIFeatures: false` → Agent Host process spawned

(Written by Copilot)

title: Fix task terminal memory leaks
body:
Summary:
- dispose task parsing, environment, decoration, and command-history resources at their lifecycle boundaries
- load the line-data addon only once when task output listeners are repeatedly attached

Validation:
- 37-run task-run leak measurement: zero growth entries
- build-fast, ESLint, and Node unit tests pass
- smoke tests: 54 passing; 7 unrelated chat-sandbox timeouts; 63 skipped
author: SimonSiefke
review_comments: [{'user': 'Copilot', 'body': '`clearBuffer()` only clears the rich command-detection history, but every shell-integration addon also installs `PartialCommandDetectionCapability` (`shellIntegrationAddon.ts:369`). That capability retains its own marker array and only trims it when a CSI erase sequence is parsed; calling `raw.clear()` does not invoke that parser handler. As a result, programmatic clears leave stale partial-command markers retained and available to mark navigation. Please expose the same clear operation on `IPartialCommandDetectionCapability` and invoke it here as well.', 'created_at': '2026-07-21T23:35:19+00:00', 'path': 'src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/browser/xterm/xtermTerminal.ts', 'position': 4}]

title: Preserve Agent Host turn identity after cancellation
body:
Fixes #326788

Late provider events from a cancelled turn were rewritten to the newest active turn ID. A stale completion could therefore finish the replacement turn before its real response arrived, causing that response to be dropped.

This change:
- preserves producer turn IDs for top-level chat actions and drops stale actions before state mutation or side effects
- retains intentional turn-ID remapping for subagent chats
- accepts provider-initiated turn starts and historical truncation actions
- prevents a cancelled turn's late completion from draining queued work
- adds regression coverage for response content, usage, tool tracking, changesets, provider-started turns, and subagents

To test:
- `npm run typecheck-client`
- `scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentSideEffects.test.ts`
- `npm run valid-layers-check`

title: AH: fix subagent resource handling
body:
## Summary

Fixes inconsistent live rendering and grouping of Agent Host subagents.

Agent Host delegated tasks begin as streaming tool calls. Their initial `toolCallStart` action already includes:

- `toolKind: 'subagent'`
- The subagent description and agent name
- The `subagentChatUri` resource

The streaming adapter previously discarded this metadata until `toolCallReady`. As a result, the parent task could initially render as a generic tool. Child tools arriving from the subagent resource could then render separately or in the wrong position.

Reloading appeared to fix the issue because restored history was reconstructed from finalized tool metadata.

This change:

- Preserves subagent metadata when the streaming invocation is first created.
- Uses the `subagentChatUri` to subscribe to the child chat resource.
- Applies consistent handling to server and client-provided delegated tasks.
- Groups child tool calls under the correct parent subagent.
- Keeps live rendering consistent with restored session rendering.

## Testing

- Added coverage verifying streaming invocations retain subagent metadata before `toolCallReady`.
- Added coverage for client-provided delegated tasks and child-resource observation.
- Added coverage verifying child tools are grouped under the parent subagent.

title: Fix: apply chat.defaultModel default on every new local chat session
body:
Fixes #326877


### Problem
`chat.defaultModel` was inconsistent between the Local chat harness and the Agents (AHP) harness. In Local sessions, after picking a different model and sending a request, creating a new chat would carry over the previous session's model instead of resetting to the configured default — only a window reload restored it. AHP behaved correctly.

### Root cause
Both harnesses share the pure precedence logic in modelSelection.ts, but drive it differently:

**AHP** (sessionModelSelectionModel.ts → transitionModelSelection) re-pushes the configured default on every new chat key, so a new conversation always resets to the default unless the user explicitly picked a model within that same chat.

**Local** (chatInputPart.ts) only applied the configured-default override on the empty-input draft path — i.e. when the freshly bound input model had no state. When a new chat's input model already carried a spilled-over selection, none of the override paths fired, and _applyConfiguredDefaultForEmptySession() wasn't triggered on a plain session switch. Reload worked only because construction re-runs initSelectedModel().

### Fix
Call the existing, already-guarded _applyConfiguredDefaultForEmptySession() from handleViewModelChange, after the incoming view model has been assigned. This is required because the helper resolves and validates the model through getCurrentSessionType(), which only reflects the incoming session once ChatWidget assigns the new view model (setInputModel runs before that). Running it there also lets reconcileSessionTypeForViewModelChange (which re-runs initSelectedModel on a genuine type change) settle first, and placing it after the transaction restores normal persistence. 

New intended behavior (both local and AHP):

- New session → configured default (chat.defaultModel) always wins, even over a spillover selection.
- Reopened conversation (non-empty) → no-op; the saved per-conversation model is restored.
- Setting unset → no-op; existing sticky "last-used model" behavior is preserved.

title: Fix automation startup readiness race
body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Agents Window automations can be claimed during startup before the requested session type or model catalog is ready. That transient state currently records a failed run and advances the schedule, causing an otherwise valid automation to be missed.

## Changes

- preflight the exact provider and session type before recording a run, leaving unavailable scheduled work due
- retry deferred work when session-type availability changes
- wait for an explicitly requested model using model, provider, session-type, cancellation, and disposal signals
- publish the first authoritative model-catalog result even when it is empty, so consumers can distinguish pending from unavailable
- clean up provisional sessions when readiness fails or is cancelled

Readiness is intentionally event-driven and has no arbitrary startup delay or timeout.

## Testing

- `npm run typecheck-client`
- `npm run valid-layers-check`
- hygiene checks
- targeted AutomationRunner, AutomationScheduler, SessionsManagementService, and language model unit tests

title: Hide the editor caret while dictation is active
body:
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a6ff4029-0e55-4edd-bac6-9732d8ab7b16


During dictation the caret is parked at the start of the dictated region (see `LiveTranscriptInserter.update` in `dictationSession.ts`), so a blinking cursor there is distracting as transcript text streams in.

This hides the caret for the duration of the dictation session by toggling a `dictation-hide-cursor` CSS class on the target editor's DOM node (added in `startDictation`, removed via the session `disposables`). A scoped rule in `dictationSession.css` hides `.cursors-layer > .cursor` only for that editor.

- Change is scoped to the editor being dictated into; other editors are unaffected.
- Fully reversible: the class is removed when the session ends (final transcript, cancel, editor disposal, or service error).

title: Fix voice mode multi-window auto-listen and cross-session glow
body:
Fixes microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#8507
Fixes microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#8514

## two windows both listen/reply in hands-free
Each window builds its own `IVoiceSessionController` (per-window `Delayed` singleton) with its own WebSocket, so when voice mode is active in more than one window (e.g. an editor window and the agents window), every window re-armed hands-free auto-listen and answered simultaneously.

**Fix:** gate the hands-free re-arm paths on this window having OS focus. Added `_isWindowFocused()` (`this._window.document.hasFocus()`) and applied it to `_enterAutoListen('auto')` and `_startBargeInListen()`. Connect-time arming (`source === 'connect'`) is a user gesture in the focused window and is left ungated. Only the focused window keeps listening; single-window behavior is unchanged.

## listening glow appears on the wrong session's input
The glow target was locked at connect time to `chatWidgetService.lastFocusedWidget` (a cross-window focused-widget singleton), so it stuck on the originally-focused pane and didn't follow session switches — glowing a background/non-active session while the correct pane showed the "Listening..." placeholder.

**Fix:** target each pane's own input container and gate the glow on the same per-session ownership the transcript overlay already computes (`voiceUiOwner = targetSession ?? ownerSession`). The glow now renders only on the input of the session voice is actually bound to, always matching the transcript overlay. Removed the now-unused locked-glow-widget autorun and `getActiveInputContainer`.

## Validation
- `npm run typecheck-client` ✅
- `npm run valid-layers-check` ✅

title: Show a plain spinner while dictation is starting
body:
### Problem

When the on-device dictation model is already downloaded (the common case), clicking the dictation mic gave **no feedback** during microphone acquisition + session open. `isPreparingModel` stayed `false`, so the toolbar button sat as a static mic until it abruptly jumped to "Listening…". Only the first-time download path showed any affordance (the determinate download ring).

### Fix

Mirror Voice Mode's `agentsVoice.connecting` pattern:

- New context key **`chatSpeechToTextStarting`**, set the moment dictation is triggered and cleared once we are actually listening (or once the determinate download ring takes over).
- New **`ChatSpeechToTextConnectingAction`** renders a plain auto-spinning `Codicon.loading` during that window.
- The toggle mic is hidden while starting/preparing; the download ring still wins when a real download is in progress, so the two spinner affordances never show together.

Wired in `chatSpeechToTextService.ts` (`start()`, `_setPreparingModel`, `_teardown`) so the state is race-free across the mic → session-open → listening transitions and every failure/cancel path.

### Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client` ✅
- eslint ✅ on all changed files

_Note: the pre-commit hygiene hook is broken in my local environment (`gulp-sort` missing from `node_modules`), unrelated to this change._

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
author: meganrogge

The toolbar therefore remains on “Starting Dictation…” permanently after a denied permission or device error. Clear the starting state in this failure path.', 'created_at': '2026-07-21T18:08:48+00:00', 'path': 'src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/speechToText/chatSpeechToTextService.ts', 'position': 65}, {'user': 'Copilot', 'body': 'This makes the new spinner a cancellation control while `service.start()` may still be awaiting `getUserMedia`. `cancelDictation()` tears down the service, but that pending `start()` has no cancellation/generation check; once permission resolves it continues into `_startLocalSession()` and Recording after `_active` was cleared, leaving a live microphone with no stop UI. Either make this indicator a no-op like `agentsVoice.connecting`, or make `start()` cancellation-aware and stop any stream returned after cancellation.', 'created_at': '2026-07-21T18:08:48+00:00', 'path': 'src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/actions/chatSpeechToTextActions.ts', 'position': 53}]

title: Prevent transient double border in Modern UI
body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

The Modern UI editor card could transiently render its border alongside the legacy editor depth shadow during layout changes.

![Intermittent double border](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/37cf61f3-d3d3-4bc7-952f-929cedf908d2)

- **Root cause**
  - Positional depth-shadow selectors could outrank the Modern UI shadow suppression rule.
- **Change**
  - Scope shadow suppression through `.monaco-grid-view`, ensuring the editor card consistently renders one stroke across sidebar and panel layouts.

## Verification steps

1. Enable `workbench.experimental.modernUI` and use a light theme.
2. Move the primary side bar between left and right.
3. Move the panel through left, right, top, and bottom.
4. Confirm the editor card retains a single border without an adjacent inset shadow.

title: Fix Voice Mode keybinding in Agents window
body:
Fixes microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#8428
Fixes microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#8517

## Problem

The Voice Mode shortcut (Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+Space) did not work reliably in the Agents window:

- **New-session view (#8428):** the shortcut did nothing — logs showed `From 3 keybinding entries, no when clauses matched the context.`
- **Linux (#8517):** the Ctrl+Alt+Shift+Space variant produced alt-modifier side effects (e.g. the terminal `+` button flipping to the split icon while Alt is held).

## Root cause

The workbench `agentsVoice.startVoiceInChat` keybinding is scoped to the `inChatInput` context key. Active sessions use the full `ChatWidget`, which sets `inChatInput`, but the **new-session composer** (`NewChatInputWidget`) is not an `IChatWidget` and never sets it — so the chord matched no when-clause there.

The earlier Linux Alt override (PR #325685) misdiagnosed #8428 as a chord conflict with parameter hints. Parameter hints only bind when a signature-help provider is present, which the chat input never has, so no conflict actually exists — and the Alt chord introduced #8517.

## Changes

- **`newChatInput.ts`**: re-bind Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+Space to `agentsVoice.startVoiceInChat` in the sessions layer, scoped to `sessionsChatInputHasDictationFocus && config.agents.voice.enabled`. The command id is preserved so push-to-talk hold mode keeps working.
- **`agentsVoice.contribution.ts`**: drop the Linux Ctrl+Alt+Shift+Space overrides on `startVoiceInChat` and `pushToTalk` so all platforms use Ctrl+Shift+Space.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client` ✅
- `npm run valid-layers-check` ✅
- pre-commit hygiene hook ✅

title: Adopt AHP 0.7.0 workingDirectories + primaryWorkingDirectory in agent host
body:
## Summary

Syncs the generated agent host protocol copy to spec version **0.6.0** (`agent-host-protocol` @ `11f1a65e`), which renames the singular `workingDirectory` on session/chat state to a `workingDirectories` array in preparation for multiroot session support.

This is milestone 1 of multiroot support: a **pure, behaviour-preserving property adoption**. Sessions continue to use a single working directory — no user-visible change.

## What changed

- **Generated protocol (14 files):** re-synced to spec 0.6.0 via `scripts/sync-agent-host-protocol.ts`. The singular `workingDirectory` is replaced by `workingDirectories?: URI[]` on the session/chat state and summary types. (`.ahp-version` → `11f1a65e`.)
- **Consumers (39 files):** mechanical migration of the renamed property:
  - reads that consume a single directory → `x.workingDirectories?.[0]`
  - field-copy / passthrough sites → whole-array passthrough (`x.workingDirectories`)
  - object-literal writes from a single URI → `dir ? [dir] : undefined` (or `[dir]` in tests)

## Explicitly *not* in this PR

No multiroot client support is added here — no capability advertising (`multipleWorkingDirectories`), no `workingDirectorySet`/`workingDirectoryRemoved` state actions, no multi-folder workspaces, and no UI. Those land in a follow-up milestone.

## Validation

- `tsc --project ./src/tsconfig.json --noEmit` — clean
- `npm run valid-layers-check` — clean
- Pre-commit hygiene hook — passed

> Note: the singular `workingDirectory` on the pre-session config commands (`ResolveSessionConfigParams`, `SessionConfigCompletionsParams`) is intentionally retained — those resolve config before a session exists and are single-context by design.

## Follow-up

Once the spec PR (microsoft/agent-host-protocol#337) merges, repoint `.ahp-version`/sync source from the spec-branch commit to the merged commit.

['Adopt AHP 0.6.0 workingDirectories property in agent host

Sync the generated agent host protocol copy to spec version 0.6.0
(agent-host-protocol @ 11f1a65e), which renames the singular
`workingDirectory` on session/chat state to a `workingDirectories`
array in preparation for multiroot session support.

This change is a pure, behaviour-preserving property adoption across all
consumers: sessions continue to use a single working directory. Reads of
a single directory now use `workingDirectories?.[0]`, field-copy sites
pass the array through unchanged, and writes from a single URI produce a
one-element array. No multiroot client support is added here (no

title: Filter Copilot config-action slash commands by session state
body:
## Summary

Filters the Copilot config-action slash command completions so that toggle forms which would be a no-op given the session's current state are hidden.

### Behavior
- **Autopilot** (symmetric toggle):
  - In autopilot → hide \`/autopilot on\`, show \`/autopilot off\`
  - Not in autopilot → show \`/autopilot on\`, hide \`/autopilot off\`
  - The \`/autopilot <objective>\` prompt form is **always** shown
- **Yolo / allow-all / autoApprove** (all aliases on the \`autoApprove\` axis):
  - Already bypassing → hide the bypass forms (\`/yolo\`, \`/yolo on\`, …), show \`/yolo off\`
  - Not bypassing → show the bypass forms, hide \`/yolo off\`
- When the current state is unknown, all forms are offered (safe default).

### Changes
- \`copilotConfigSlashCommands.ts\` — added \`ICopilotConfigSlashCommandState\`, a \`shouldOfferOption\` filter (prompt/keep-text forms always kept; pure toggles hidden when a no-op on their axis), and an optional \`state\` parameter on \`getCopilotConfigSlashCommandItems\`.
- \`copilotSlashCommandCompletionProvider.ts\` — added \`getSessionConfigState?\` to \`ICopilotSlashCommandSessionInfo\` and passes resolved state into the item builder.
- \`copilotAgent.ts\` — implemented \`_getSessionConfigState\`, reading effective \`mode\`/\`autoApprove\` via \`IAgentConfigurationService.getEffectiveValue\`, and wired it into the provider.
- Added tests covering autopilot and autoApprove state filtering.

### Verification
- \`npm run typecheck-client\` — passes
- ESLint on changed files — clean
- Unit tests — 6 passing (including the 2 new state-filtering tests)

title: Capture mic via AudioWorkletNode instead of deprecated ScriptProcessorNode (dictation + Voice Mode)
body:
### Problem

Audio capture for chat dictation and Voice Mode used `ctx.createScriptProcessor(...)`, which is deprecated:

> [Deprecation] The ScriptProcessorNode is deprecated. Use AudioWorkletNode instead.

Its `onaudioprocess` callback runs on the **main thread**, where it gets throttled or stops firing entirely (the Voice Mode path already kept a fallback drain timer for exactly this reason). When it stops, no PCM is streamed and dictation silently produces nothing.

### Change

Replace `ScriptProcessorNode` with an `AudioWorkletNode`, which runs on the dedicated audio rendering thread:

- New shared helper `chat/browser/pcmCaptureWorklet.ts` (`createPcmCaptureNode`) loads a PCM-capture worklet from a `blob:` URL (allowed by the renderer's `script-src` CSP) and invokes a callback with each fixed-size mono chunk on the main thread.
- **Chat dictation** (`chatSpeechToTextService.ts`): captures 4096-sample chunks, encodes to PCM16 and streams them. `_startCapture` is now async with a `this._audioContext !== ctx` teardown guard.
- **Voice Mode mic capture** (`voiceClient/micCaptureService.ts`): captures 2048-sample chunks to match the previous ScriptProcessorNode buffer size, so the per-chunk drain/diagnostic bookkeeping is unchanged. Includes a `this._micCtx !== ctx` guard if capture is stopped while the module loads.

### Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client` passes cleanly.
- Pre-commit hygiene hooks ran (no `--no-verify`).

title: Show focus differentiator for ask-questions checkbox navigation
body:
Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/321134


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4e797014-ea84-45d8-a58f-5358581cfd8d


## Problem

In the ask-questions carousel, multi-select (checkbox) rows are navigated with the up/down arrow keys by moving DOM focus. However the stylesheet applies `.chat-question-list-item:focus { outline: none; }`, and — unlike single-select, which moves its `.selected` background as you navigate — checkbox rows had no visual state tied to focus. As a result, the currently focused checkbox item had no differentiator during keyboard navigation.

## Fix

Added a focus indicator scoped to multi-select rows in `chatQuestionCarousel.css`:

```css
.chat-question-list-item.multi-select:focus {
	outline: 1px solid var(--vscode-focusBorder);
	outline-offset: -1px;
}
```

- Nested inside `.chat-question-list`, so it out-specifies the `outline: none` rule.
- Uses `--vscode-focusBorder` (matching the freeform textarea's focus treatment; works in high-contrast themes).
- Gated on `.multi-select`, so single-select rows are unaffected.

title: Dictation: download Foundry Local native runtime on demand
body:
Re-applies #326678 (on-device dictation via Foundry Local streaming ASR) **without shipping its native payload**, so we keep VS Code's minimum supported Linux glibc floor (Ubuntu 20 / Debian 10 / RHEL 8).

## Problem
#326678 bundled `foundry-local-sdk`'s prebuilt N-API addon (`foundry_local_napi.node`) and native core libraries. The addon requires `GLIBC_2.34` (verified on both `linux-x64` and `linux-arm64` via `.gnu.version_r`). The Linux dependency generator scans every shipped `.node` and would declare `libc6 (>= 2.34)`, raising the floor for the **entire product** and dropping Ubuntu 20 / Debian 10-11 / RHEL 8. It was reverted in #326769.

The ONNX Runtime / Foundry Core `.so` libraries themselves satisfy the current floor — only the addon is the problem.

## Approach — download the native runtime on demand
Rather than raise the whole-product glibc floor for an experimental feature, the native runtime is downloaded on demand at runtime, only on supported platforms, into a per-user writable cache. The GLIBC_2.34 addon is never in the scanned/declared package, so the floor is intact.

- **Packaging (`build/`)** — exclude every `foundry-local-sdk/prebuilds/**` and `foundry-local-core/**` from the package; drop the build-time core fetch (`ensureFoundryLocalCorePackage` / `build/lib/foundryLocal.ts`), the Linux dep-generator soname additions, and the darwin universal/macho skip entries.
- **SDK loader patch (`build/npm/postinstall.ts`)** — patch the SDK's `dist/detail/coreInterop.js` to honor `VSCODE_FOUNDRY_LOCAL_NATIVE_DIR` for both addon and core-library resolution, falling back to the original package-relative logic so dev-from-source still works. Idempotent; warns (does not fail) if the SDK's loader shape changes.
- **Runtime downloader (`src/vs/platform/localTranscription/node/foundryLocalRuntime.ts`)** — before loading the SDK, ensure the addon (extracted from the pinned `foundry-local-sdk` npm tarball) and the core libraries (via the SDK's own NuGet installer `runInstall`, targeted at the cache with its `binDir` option) are present, then point the loader at the cache via the env var. Version-stamped by SDK version, idempotent (`.complete` marker), and de-duped across concurrent sessions.

Cache layout mirrors the SDK package layout so the loader patch is a trivial path join:

```
<cacheHome>/chatDictationRuntime/<sdkVersion>/prebuilds/<rid>/foundry_local_napi.node
<cacheHome>/chatDictationRuntime/<sdkVersion>/foundry-local-core/<rid>/<core libs>
```

The **model** itself continues to download on demand at first use (unchanged).

## Proxy support
All three provisioning download legs honor a configured proxy:
- The npm-registry addon tarball (our own fetch) and the NuGet core libraries (via the SDK's bundled installer) read the standard proxy environment variables (`HTTPS_PROXY` / `HTTP_PROXY` / `ALL_PROXY`, with `NO_PROXY`) — our fetch attaches an `HttpsProxyAgent`, and the SDK's bare `https.get` calls are routed by temporarily pointing `https.globalAgent` at it (restored afterwards, no SDK patching). This matches how the GitHub desktop app's Rust `foundry-local-sdk` (reqwest/ureq) reaches the same endpoints.
- VS Code's `http.proxy` / `http.noProxy` **settings** are bridged into the dictation utility process and applied as those same environment variables before any download, so a proxy configured only in VS Code (not in the OS environment) is honored — including by the native Foundry Local **model** download, which reads OS-level/env proxy the same way.
- `http.proxyAuthorization` (a `Basic <base64>` value) is folded into the proxy URL's credentials, so both our fetches and the native model download authenticate to the proxy. `http.proxyStrictSSL: false` disables TLS certificate verification for the Node download legs (scoped to the dedicated dictation utility process).

TLS-intercepting proxies otherwise rely on the CA certificate being present in the OS trust store (matching `@vscode/proxy-agent` and the desktop app). Non-`Basic` proxy auth schemes (e.g. Negotiate/NTLM), and disabling TLS verification for the native model leg, are left to OS-level configuration.

## Also in this PR
Un-reverting #326678 also restores these related changes it originally made:
- Removes the `@huggingface/transformers` dependency and deletes the `build/npm/stubs/sharp/` stub it required.
- Deletes the prior on-device transcriber path (`nemotronTranscriber.ts`, ~797 lines), superseded by Foundry Local streaming ASR.
- Bumps `tar` `^7.5.16` → `^7.5.20`, kept in sync with the root `package.json` / lockfile for the hygiene check.

## Supported platforms
-  `darwin-arm64`, `linux-x64`, `linux-arm64`, `win32-x64`, `win32-arm64` (mirrors the SDK RID map and the existing dictation gate).

Un-reverts #326678. Refs #326769.

(`foundry_local_napi.node`) and native core libraries. The addon requires
GLIBC_2.34 (verified on linux-x64 and linux-arm64), which the Linux
dependency generator scans and declares as `libc6 (>= 2.34)`, dropping our
minimum supported distros for the whole product. It was reverted in #326769.

Instead of bundling, the native runtime is now downloaded on demand at
runtime, only on supported platforms, into a per-user writable cache:

- Runtime downloader (`foundryLocalRuntime.ts`): before loading the SDK,

Note: downloads use plain https and do not honor VS Code proxy settings,
matching the SDK's bundled installer and the Foundry Local model download.

and runtime `require` resolution were verified against the installed SDK.

title: Dictation: make redundant-extension prompt sticky and mark shown only after response
body:
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5b7f7377-fec2-456e-87a5-fb60e52e09a5

### Problem

The prompt to disable the redundant `ms-vscode.vscode-speech` extension (added in #326665) could silently never appear:

- It uses a **non-sticky** `Severity.Info` notification, which auto-hides after a few seconds (only error-with-action and progress notifications are sticky).
- It calls `markShown()` — burning the once-per-machine `StorageScope.APPLICATION` flag — **before** the prompt is shown, regardless of outcome.

On Insiders, `chat.speechToText.enabled` defaults to `true`, so the notifier fires on the first eligible launch. If the transient toast appeared while the user wasn't looking, it auto-dismissed and the flag was permanently set — so it never showed again.

### Changes

- Add `sticky: true` so the notification stays until the user responds.
- Move `markShown()` into each choice's `run`/`onCancel` so the flag is only burned once the user has actually acted on the prompt.
- Bump the storage key to `.v2` so machines that already burned the old flag get one more chance to see the (now sticky) prompt.

commit_messages:
["Dictation: make redundant-extension prompt sticky and mark shown only after response

The prompt to disable the redundant VS Code Speech extension used a
non-sticky Severity.Info notification and burned its once-per-machine
flag *before* the prompt was shown. On Insiders (where
chat.speechToText.enabled defaults to true) it could fire as a transient
toast, auto-dismiss unseen, and never appear again.

- Add sticky: true so the notification stays until the user responds.
- Move markShown() into each choice's run/onCancel so the flag is only
  burned once the user has actually acted on the prompt.
- Bump the storage key to .v2 so machines that already burned the old
  flag get one more chance to see the (now sticky) prompt.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
Copilot-Session: 0e880d06-9ed1-4131-9b77-3766bbec6977", "Address review: exclude env-enabled ext, coordinate prompt across windows

- Exclude EnabledByEnvironment from the eligibility check; setEnablement
  cannot disable environment-enabled extensions, so the primary action
  would be guaranteed to fail.
- Add multi-window coordination: since the once-per-machine flag is now
  recorded only after the user responds, every open window could show its
  own prompt. Listen for the app-scoped flag and close this window's
  prompt when any other window records a response.
- Remove comments that merely restate sticky:true / markShown().

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
Copilot-Session: 0e880d06-9ed1-4131-9b77-3766bbec6977"]

## Summary

- add 42 shared bundled-provider E2E scenarios for multi-chat capability, peer lifecycle, local commands, workspace tools, provider context isolation/resume/reset, attachments, completions, titles, disposal, and fork behavior
- assert actual normalized replay requests carry prior user/assistant context and attachment projections instead of trusting sequence-only replay responses
- add strict generated Claude and Copilot fixtures while keeping host-only scenarios on the shared empty capture
- add a persistent inventory and reevaluation process for all disabled or conditional bundled-provider E2E tests
- document the public strategy for future coverage-guided Agent Host E2E expansion rounds
- refresh loaded-file native V8 coverage metrics

## Coverage

Compared with current `main`:

- lines/statements: 69.92% -> 71.07% (+1.15 pp, +1353 covered)
- functions: 58.84% -> 61.64% (+2.80 pp, +98 covered)
- branches: 62.35% -> 63.25% (+0.90 pp, +383 covered)

The second expansion within this PR contributed +116 covered lines/statements, +8 functions, and +100 branches over the rebased PR baseline.

## Provider notes

- Claude and Copilot cover peer-chat lifecycle, workspace tools, provider context, and attachment projection
- Codex explicitly verifies that multi-chat is not advertised/supported
- Claude still advertises fork support, but provider-context fork tests are skipped because the SDK reproducibly rejects the AHP turn id as `upToMessageId`
- one default-to-fresh-peer context-isolation scenario is Copilot-only because Claude's shared SDK process reproducibly loses its in-process `host` MCP server after the preceding peer-lifecycle sequence; the remaining context-isolation scenarios run on both providers
- Copilot peer edit/nested-create variants are skipped on Windows because their recorded tool plans use POSIX shell behavior and do not produce the expected Windows filesystem effects

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client`
- full Claude provider replay: 93 passing, 7 expected pending
- strict host-only recording check: 6 passing, 3 expected pending, no new captures
- `npm run test-agent-host-e2e-coverage`: 231 passing, 73 expected pending
- `npm run valid-layers-check`
- focused replay for the Windows-gated peer mutations: 4 passing, 2 expected pending
- precommit hygiene, fixture redaction checks, mechanical disabled-test inventory audit, and final code review

(Written by Copilot)

it across the whole suite. After enough sessions that subprocess degrades

though replay is instant), which times out and, via teardown of the

ECONNREFUSED. Proactively recycle the server every 25 tests, and restart
it after any failed test so a wedge cannot cascade into unrelated tests.

title: fix: decouple embeddings registration guard from main-thread model snapshot (fixes #326819)
body:
### Summary `ExtHostEmbeddings.registerEmbeddingsProvider` throws `An embeddings provider for this model is already registered` even when the extension host holds no live registration for that model. The dedup guard (`_allKnownModels`) is shared with the asynchronous main-thread model snapshot delivered via `$acceptEmbeddingModels`. An in-flight/stale snapshot can re-populate a model id that the extension host has already locally unregistered, so the very next `registerEmbeddingsProvider` for that model — commonly the Copilot Chat embeddings provider re-registering on an authentication change — trips the guard. Impact: the Copilot Chat embeddings provider fails to register, so semantic/embeddings features silently break for the affected session and an unhandled error is reported. Fixes microsoft/vscode#326819 Recommended reviewer: `@jrieken` ### Culprit Commit | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | Commit | [`6eaf6487`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/6eaf6487a4d8301b981036bfa53976546eb6694f) | | Author | `@jrieken` | | PR | #219994 | | Message | make sure to reset known embeddings models | | Why | This commit made `$acceptEmbeddingModels` replace `_allKnownModels` with the main-thread snapshot while that same set was left doubling as the local registration dedup guard. Because registration never adds to the set and disposal deletes from it, a late-arriving snapshot re-adds a just-unregistered model and the guard on the next register throws. | > This is a latent core defect (July 2024), an ancestor of the shipped build `8a7abeba`. The recent-regression telemetry signal comes from the Copilot Chat extension (0.57.0) re-registering the embeddings provider on every `onDidAuthenticationChange`, which exercises the register-after-dispose path that exposes the pre-existing race. The fix belongs in core, where the unreliable guard state is produced. ### Code Flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Ext as CopilotChat _registerEmbeddings participant EH as ExtHostEmbeddings participant Main as MainThreadEmbeddings Ext->>EH: register copilot.model (auth valid) EH->>Main: $registerEmbeddingProvider Main-->>EH: $acceptEmbeddingModels([copilot.model]) Note over EH: _allKnownModels = {copilot.model} Ext->>EH: dispose (auth change) Note over EH: _allKnownModels.delete(copilot.model) Main-->>EH: stale $acceptEmbeddingModels([copilot.model]) Note over EH: ⚠️ guard re-populated {copilot.model}
while no live registration exists Ext->>EH: register copilot.model (auth valid again) Note over EH: 💥 An embeddings provider for this model is already registered ``` ### Affected Files | File | Role | Evidence | |------|------|----------| | `src/vs/workbench/api/common/extHostEmbedding.ts` | Root cause + crash site | L32-34 threw off `_allKnownModels`, which L90 (`$acceptEmbeddingModels`) reassigns from the async main-thread snapshot: `this._allKnownModels = new Set(models)`. The guard and the snapshot were the same variable. | | `src/vs/workbench/api/browser/mainThreadEmbeddings.ts` | Producer of snapshot | L88-90: `onDidChange` fires `$acceptEmbeddingModels(Array.from(allProviders))` on every provider add/remove, sending racy snapshots to the extension host. | | `extensions/copilot/src/extension/conversation/vscode-node/languageModelAccess.ts` | Trigger | L546-575 `_registerEmbeddings`/`update` clears and re-registers the same `copilot.${model}` provider on every `onDidAuthenticationChange`, exercising the register-after-dispose path. | ### Repro Steps 1. Sign in so the Copilot Chat embeddings provider registers `copilot.text-embedding-3-small` (main thread broadcasts the model snapshot back). 2. Trigger an authentication change (token refresh / re-auth) so `_registerEmbeddings.update()` disposes the current registration and re-registers the same model. 3. When a previously-sent `$acceptEmbeddingModels` snapshot containing the model is delivered to the extension host after the local dispose but before the re-register, the guard still reports the model as present. 4. The re-register throws `An embeddings provider for this model is already registered`. ### How the Fix Works **Chosen approach** (`src/vs/workbench/api/common/extHostEmbedding.ts`): Introduce a dedicated `_registeredModels` set that is the single source of truth for the local dedup guard — `registerEmbeddingsProvider` adds to it on register and the returned disposable deletes from it on dispose. The guard check (and the throw) now consult `_registeredModels`, which is mutated only synchronously alongside the actual provider map, so it can never be clobbered by an asynchronous message. `_allKnownModels` is left to do exactly one job: hold the main-thread snapshot backing the public `embeddingsModels` getter, updated by `$acceptEmbeddingModels`. This fixes the producer of the invalid guard state (the shared, racily-overwritten variable) rather than guarding at the crash site; no `try/catch` is added and no error logging is removed, so the telemetry path is unchanged for genuine duplicate registrations. **Alternatives considered**: - Wrapping the extension's re-register in `try/catch` — rejected because it hides the core state bug instead of fixing the data producer, and would silently leave the embeddings provider unregistered. - Having the extension skip re-registration when the model is unchanged — reduces churn but leaves the core guard racy for any other consumer, so it treats the trigger rather than the root cause. ### Recommended Owner `@jrieken` — authored the embeddings extension host API and the `$acceptEmbeddingModels` reset logic that produced the shared guard state; core VS Code maintainer for the extension host API surface. > Generated by [errors-fix](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-engineering/actions/runs/29843485978) · 2.4K AIC · ⌖ 34.4 AIC · ⊞ 71K · [◷](https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Amicrosoft%2Fvscode+%22gh-aw-workflow-id%3A+errors-fix%22&type=pullrequests) --- ### errors-fix-driver — cycle 1 **Trigger**: cron_review_comments · **Head**: `97698102731e599d8b66c93183b133bf08215d19` (`9769810`) | Item | Action | |------|--------| | Review on `extHostEmbedding.ts:41` — add before register (in scope) | Fixed in `9769810` (replied + resolved) | | Review on `extHostEmbedding.ts:41` — inconsistent state on throw (in scope) | Fixed in `9769810` (replied + resolved) | | Review on `extHostEmbedding.ts:34` — name model in error (in scope) | Fixed in `9769810` (replied + resolved) | **Push**: yes — `9769810` · **Copilot rerequested**: ok **Ready gate**: CI + Copilot re-review pending on new head → not marking ready this cycle > Generated by [errors-fix-driver](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-engineering/actions/runs/29846230984) · 679.7 AIC · ⌖ 33.7 AIC · ⊞ 72.9K · [◷](https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Amicrosoft%2Fvscode+%22gh-aw-workflow-call-id%3A+microsoft%2Fvscode-engineering%2Ferrors-fix-driver%22&type=pullrequests)

title: Add a when clause context key for detecting if an extension is installed+enabled
body:
Fixes #326815.

This PR adds a when clause context key for detecting if an extension is installed+enabled. This is useful in cases where you want to hide something (e.g. a duplicate view or command, etc.), but do not control the other extension, or do not want to rely on it being activated first.

Submitting as a draft for now, due to ongoing feed issues I cannot actually do `npm install` locally.

title: Config-action slash commands for Copilot agent-host chat inputs
body:
Fixes #325890

## What & why

In Copilot agent-host chat sessions, typing a permission/mode slash command (e.g. `/plan`) did **not** update the mode/permission pickers. This PR introduces **config-action slash commands** that toggle a session-config axis instead of sending a chat turn, and wires them into **both** the editor-window chat input and the Agents window.

Typing `/` now offers, for Copilot agent-host sessions only:

- **Permissions axis (`autoApprove`):** `/yolo`, `/yolo on|off`, `/allow-all`, `/autoApprove`
- **Mode axis (`mode`):** `/autopilot on|off`, `/autopilot <objective>`, `/plan <prompt>`, `/goal`

Selecting an item toggles the corresponding session config and the picker updates reactively; it does not send a chat turn.

## How it works

- **Producer (server):** the Copilot completion provider emits these items with an `action` bag (`{ applyConfig }`) on the completion attachment `_meta`. Runtime commands that collide (e.g. `plan`) are shadowed.
- **Consumer (client, shared across both windows):** a shared accept-handler runs the existing elevated-permission confirmation (`maybeConfirmElevatedPermissionLevel`) for elevated `autoApprove` values, then applies the change via a per-window seam — editor uses the AHP dispatch/provisional path; the Agents window uses `provider.setSessionConfigValue`.
- **Insert behavior:** toggle items insert nothing (`insertText: ''` + explicit `label`); `<prompt>` items keep `/cmd ` and show an argument hint.
- **Send path:** `CopilotAgentSession.send` intercepts these commands, re-applies the mode, and strips the leading token so it is not dispatched to the runtime.
- **Policy:** elevated auto-approve items are omitted when enterprise policy disables global auto-approval (client-side, mirroring the pickers), with clamps kept as defense-in-depth.
- **Cleanup:** the old hardcoded permission commands in `chatSlashCommands.ts` are unscoped from agent-host Copilot sessions so the completion pipeline solely owns them.

## Tests

- `agentMetaReaders` — round-trip of the new `action` `_meta`.
- `copilotConfigSlashCommands` — catalog items + send-path resolver.
- `CopilotSlashCommandCompletionProvider` — config items injected, runtime collision shadowing.
- `applyAgentHostCompletionAction` — elevated confirmation gating + policy-block predicate.

Validation: `typecheck-client`, `valid-layers-check`, ESLint, and the affected unit suites all pass.

## Known follow-ups (not in this PR)

A review flagged a few items to address separately: applying `autoApprove` on the manually-typed send path, avoiding empty turns for bare toggles, the `/goal` vs `toCopilotSdkMode('goal')` naming, tightening `_meta.action` trust, and remote-Copilot editor apply.

Capture the input-scoped session in the completion argument (or inject the scoped context) and apply against that identity.', 'created_at': '2026-07-21T13:17:24+00:00', 'path': 'src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/browser/agentHostInputCompletions.ts', 'position': 1}, {'user': 'Copilot', 'body': 'Running these updates concurrently can drop values for new sessions: `setSessionConfigValue` deliberately ignores a call while config resolution is in progress (`baseAgentHostSessionsProvider.ts:2591-2593`). title: Fix Agent Host startup race in Remote-SSH windows
body:
## Summary

- wait for the Remote-SSH environment before starting the editor-side Agent Host handshake
- provide a transport factory so later transport loss can use AHP soft reconnect
- add regression coverage for the startup ordering race

## Root cause

The editor-side Agent Host client could begin connecting while Remote-SSH authority resolution was still replacing the management connection. The stale connection then closed the one-shot AHP client before the replacement server exposed `agentHostProxy`, leaving Agent Host agents unavailable until the window was reloaded.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client`
- `npm run valid-layers-check`
- `npm run precommit`
- 58 focused Agent Host connection tests

(Written by Copilot)

title: [cherry-pick] Fix submenu rendering in modern UI
body:
Cherry-pick of #326703 from `main`.

<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Modern UI menu motion retained a transform-containing block on the scrollable menu surface, causing fixed-position submenus such as **Settings > Themes** to be clipped.

- Changes the opening animation fill mode from `both` to `backwards`.
- Restricts `will-change` to `opacity`, preventing transforms from persisting after the animation.
- Adds regression coverage for the computed menu motion styles.

title: Show all cloud sessions in the agents window regardless of active repo
body:
## Problem

In the agents window, the v2 Task backend's `fetchSessionList` scoped the cloud session list to the active workspace's repositories (via `getRepoId`). As a result, the agents window only showed sessions for the currently selected repo instead of all of the user's cloud sessions.

The `isAgentWorkspace` flag was passed to `fetchSessionList` but ignored (`_isAgentWorkspace`), so the agents window fell through to the repo-scoped code path whenever an active GitHub repo was present.

## Fix

Use the global user-scoped `agents/tasks` list when in the agents window, regardless of `repoIds`. This mirrors the existing v1 Jobs backend behavior in [`jobsApiBackend.ts`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/extensions/copilot/src/extension/chatSessions/vscode-node/jobsApiBackend.ts), which already gates on `isAgentWorkspace || !repoIds || repoIds.length === 0`.

```ts
if (isAgentWorkspace || !repoIds || repoIds.length === 0) {
    // global agents/tasks list — all the user's sessions
```

The global `agents/tasks` endpoint is already scoped to the authenticated user, so no `creator_id` filter is needed.

## Behavior

- **Agents window**: shows all of the user's cloud sessions across every repo, regardless of which folder/repo is active.
- **Outside the agents window**: unchanged — still repo-scoped via `creator_id`.

## Tests

Added a unit test asserting the agents window uses the global list (and never the repo-scoped endpoint) even when `repoIds` are present. All `fetchSessionList` tests pass.

In an agents workspace with an active repo, the displayed cache is global but polling remains repo-scoped, so it either refreshes repeatedly because the counts differ or fails to notice sessions added in another repo. Pass `vscode.workspace.isAgentSessionsWorkspace` through those calls as well (and cover the polling path), so every agents-window fetch uses the same scope.", 'created_at': '2026-07-21T00:08:00+00:00', 'path': 'extensions/copilot/src/extension/chatSessions/vscode-node/taskApiBackend.ts', 'position': 12}, {'user': 'osortega', 'body': 'Good catch. title: [cherry-pick] NES: split open-tab vs related-file neighbor context
body:
Cherry-pick of #326626 from `main`.

## Summary

Two related improvements to the **xtab (NES / Next Edit Suggestions)** *neighboring-files context*. Both hinge on distinguishing neighbor snippets that come from **open tabs** vs. from **language-service "related" files** (the non-open-tab files a language service suggests, e.g. `related/typescript`, `related/cpp`).

1. **No line numbers for related-file snippets.** Snippets sourced from language-service related files now omit line numbers in the prompt, matching NES's *own* language-context path (`appendLanguageContextSnippets`, which already uses `IncludeLineNumbersOption.None`). Open-tab neighbor snippets are unchanged and keep their line numbers.
2. **Ability to turn off the related-files context.** A new `neighborFiles.includeRelatedFiles` option lets us disable the completions-style related-files context entirely, since NES already has its own language-context implementation (`ILanguageContextProviderService`). When off, the related-files LSP computation is **skipped entirely** (no wasted work), leaving only open-tab neighbors.

Both default to **behavior-preserving** settings, so this PR is a no-op until the new config is flipped.

## Motivation

NES's neighboring-files context (Jaccard-ranked snippets from Completions) overlaps with NES's own language context. This PR makes the two coexist cleanly: related-file snippets are formatted consistently with the language-context path (no line numbers), and the redundant related-files context can be switched off per experiment.

## What changed

**Point 1 — provenance tag + line-number formatting.** Each neighbor snippet carries its provenance, decided once at the source (where the neighbor type is known) rather than re-derived from URIs:
- `neighborFiles.ts` (completions-core): `isRelatedNeighboringFileType(type)` is a `switch` over the `Related*` enum members (robust to enum changes, no string-prefix matching). `getNeighborFilesAndTraits` stamps `isFromRelatedFile` on each related doc as it is materialized.
- `prompt.ts` / `selectRelevance.ts`: `SimilarFileInfo` and `ScoredSnippet` gain an optional `isFromRelatedFile`. `getSimilarSnippets` propagates it (and the source `uri`) onto every ranked snippet and guarantees it on its return type (`SnippetWithSourceInfo`).
- `similarFilesContext.ts`: `getSnippetsForPrompt` reads `s.isFromRelatedFile` directly — no post-ranking URI set / cross-referencing.
- `similarFilesContextService.ts`: `INeighborFileSnippet` gains `readonly isFromRelatedFile: boolean`.
- `recentFilesForPrompt.ts`: `appendNeighborFileSnippets` uses `IncludeLineNumbersOption.None` for related-file snippets, else the configured option.

**Point 2 — toggle**
- `xtabPromptOptions.ts`: adds `includeRelatedFiles` to `NeighborFilesOptions` (type + `VALIDATOR` + `DEFAULT_OPTIONS`, default `true`).
- `configurationService.ts`: new team-internal, experiment-based key `chat.advanced.inlineEdits.xtabProvider.neighborFiles.includeRelatedFiles`.
- `xtabProvider.ts`: wires the config into the `neighborFiles` options and threads the flag into `getSnippetsForPrompt` and the fire-and-forget telemetry `compute`.
- `neighborFiles.ts` (completions-core): `getNeighborFilesAndTraits` gains an `includeRelatedFiles: boolean = true` param; when `false` it returns early with open-tab neighbors only, before any related-files/LSP work.

## Behavior & compatibility

- **Defaults unchanged:** `includeRelatedFiles` defaults to `true`; related files continue to be included exactly as before. Line-numbering for open-tab snippets is unchanged.
- **Only new behavior** is (a) related-file snippets drop line numbers, and (b) the new exp key can turn related files off.
- Gated correctly for AI-disabled users — this is inside the existing xtab provider path and only runs when `neighborFiles.enabled` is on.

## How to review

Suggested reading order:

1. **`similarFilesContextService.ts`** — the new `isFromRelatedFile` field + the `includeRelatedFiles` param on the two service methods. This is the contract for everything else.
2. **`neighborFiles.ts`** (completions-core) — `isRelatedNeighboringFileType`, the `isFromRelatedFile` stamp on related docs, and the one-line early-return in `getNeighborFilesAndTraits` (`if (!includeRelatedFiles || featuresService.excludeRelatedFiles(...))`). Confirm skipping related files still returns open-tab neighbors + empty traits.
3. **`similarFiles.ts` / `selectRelevance.ts`** — the tag rides on `SimilarFileInfo` → each snippet; `getSimilarSnippets` guarantees `uri` + `isFromRelatedFile` on its return type.
4. **`similarFilesContext.ts`** — `getSnippetsForPrompt` classifies purely from `s.isFromRelatedFile` (no URI set), so multi-root relative-path collisions can't misclassify a snippet.
5. **`recentFilesForPrompt.ts`** — related snippets get `IncludeLineNumbersOption.None`; open-tab snippets keep the configured option.

## Tests

- `similarFiles.test.ts` (prompt): `getSimilarSnippets` preserves each source `uri` under a multi-root relativePath collision, and propagates `isFromRelatedFile` from source file → snippet.
- `neighborFiles.test.ts` (completions-core): `includeRelatedFiles=false` retains open-tab neighbors, keeps traits empty, and (via a call counter on the mocked provider) proves the related-files provider is never invoked — with a positive control for the enabled path.
- `recentFilesForPrompt.spec.ts` (xtab): related snippets omit line numbers; open-tab snippets keep them.

title: Support Go to Symbol (⇧⌘O) for chat sessions
body:
## Summary

Makes **Go to Symbol in Editor** (`⇧⌘O` / `Ctrl+Shift+O`) work for chat, treating each user request (prompt) as a navigable "symbol" so you can jump between exchanges in a conversation. Previously the palette just showed *"To go to a symbol, first open a text editor with symbol information."* for chats.

This works for both:
- **Chat editors** — via a new `ChatOutline` registered with `IOutlineService`, which also lights up the Outline pane and Breadcrumbs for free.
- **A focused chat widget** (including the **Agents window** and the sidebar chat view) — handled directly in the quick access provider.

## What a "symbol" is

Each **user request** becomes a top-level entry, labeled with the prompt text and a chat icon. Selecting one reveals and focuses that request in the chat.

## Changes

- **`chatOutline.ts` (new)** — `ChatOutline` / `ChatOutlineCreator` implementing `IOutline`/`IOutlineCreator`, matched to the `ChatEditor` pane. Registered in `chat.shared.contribution.ts`. No changes to the Go to Symbol picker were needed for the editor case — it consumes any registered outline.
- **`gotoSymbolQuickAccess.ts`**
  - Overrides `provide()` to prioritize a **focused chat** over an active file editor, so the chat wins when it has focus even with a file open side by side (otherwise the base routes to the file editor's symbols). Focus is detected via `isAncestorOfActiveElement` on the widget DOM node, checked before the quick input steals focus.

title: Chat dictation: always use Nemotron model, remove model setting
body:
The on-device chat dictation runtime is Microsoft Foundry Local's streaming ASR engine, and the only supported model is NVIDIA Nemotron (`nemotron-speech-streaming-en-0.6b` — the model the GitHub Copilot app ships). The `chat.speechToText.model` setting therefore only ever had a single valid value, and the legacy Whisper model IDs no longer resolve.

This PR removes model selection entirely and hardcodes Nemotron:

- **Remove the `chat.speechToText.model` setting.** Its migration is replaced with one that clears any explicitly-stored value so it doesn't linger as an unknown setting (this also drops the legacy `onnx-community/whisper-*` references).
- **`ChatSpeechToTextService`**: remove `MODEL_SETTING` and `_getModelId()`; start the local session without a model argument.
- **`ILocalTranscriptionService.start()`**: drop the unused optional `model` option from the interface, the electron-browser proxy, and the node implementation. The node service always uses the Nemotron default.

No user-facing behavior change: dictation already defaulted to Nemotron. This just removes the dead selection surface and the last Whisper references.

### Validation
- `npm run typecheck-client` passes.

title: [cherry-pick] Add telemetry for applied enterprise policies
body:
Cherry-pick of #326686 from `main`.

## Summary

Adds a consolidated `policy.applied` telemetry event for understanding enterprise policy adoption.

The event:

- Fires once after workbench restoration and again when effective policy state changes.
- Debounces change bursts by 500 ms and suppresses duplicate payloads.
- Reports the total number of applied policies.
- Reports whether selected chat, plugin, OpenTelemetry, telemetry-level, and feedback policies are applied.
- Reports low-cardinality value buckets for default-model auto selection, tool auto-approval being forced off, marketplace lockdown, OTel being forced on, and telemetry level.
- Never reports raw policy values, model identifiers, organization names, plugin IDs, marketplace URLs, or other user/admin-provided strings.

The contribution reads only authoritative effective values from `IPolicyService`. Delivery-source attribution is intentionally excluded because the current policy service API does not expose which child of `MultiplexPolicyService` supplied the winning value.

Supersedes #325385, preserving Harald's original commit and simplifying the implementation from five changed files to three.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client`
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/services/policies/test/browser/policyTelemetryContribution.test.ts`
- `npm run valid-layers-check`
- VS Code hygiene checks
- `@vscode/telemetry-extractor@1.14.0`

Focused tests cover the empty startup event, every reported policy and value bucket, privacy-safe handling of unexpected values, the total applied-policy count, debounced updates, and payload deduplication.

title: agentHost: Handle subagent user messages safely
body:
## Summary

- ignore subagent `user.message` events in root steering, SDK event-boundary tracking, and instruction telemetry
- restore persisted subagent user messages as the child turn prompt instead of assistant response content
- add live and replay regression coverage

## Why

The Copilot SDK may emit `user.message` events for subagents. Without explicit `agentId` handling, those events could mutate root-turn state, associate the wrong SDK event boundary, and emit root-only instruction telemetry.

A broader audit of other SDK events carrying `agentId` is tracked in [#326710](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/326710).

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client`
- Agent Host hygiene checks
- `npm run valid-layers-check`
- focused Agent Host unit tests: 237 passing

(Written by Copilot)
author: roblourens
